articles.title: Amid Lamar Jackson's latest injury and Joe Burrow's roller-coaster day, are Steelers quietly pulling away in AFC North?
articles.summary: The Steelers appear to be finding their identity in their first year under head coach Mike McCarthy, who's reuniting with longtime Packers colleague and quar...
articles.body:
As Jaylen Warren hit a center hole and then zigged to the right, 5 yards still stood between the Pittsburgh Steelers running back and the successful conversion of a third-and-13 in the first quarter.

But Warren's teammates blocked Cleveland Browns pursuers downfield. Warren slipped behind one block and out of the grasp of another defender as he zagged back toward the middle of the field.

Not until Warren had barreled 51 yards would the Browns down him. By then, the Steelers were well on their way to a field goal that would extend Pittsburgh's lead to 10-0.

"I was running, running out of gas, then finding the next dude to make a cut," Warren said. "I try to make cuts into my blockers so I can get a blocker on my way down so that's basically what it looks like."

And on a day when the Steelers' 27-6 statement delivered them sole possession of the AFC North lead , the Steelers also found themselves facing another reality.

Like Warren's run, gaining 51 yards when they needed just more than 13, the Steelers won one game and were arguably helped as much by their other two division rivals.

Pittsburgh's recipe to win seemed as telling as the win itself.

A Steelers team that won just two of its first four, dropping a game to the same Browns team it's now beaten, has since ripped off four straight wins.

In the AFC North, they seem to have the right ingredients at the right time.

"You got to stop the run and you got to make sure you run the ball," defensive lineman Cam Heyward said after tallying 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss, one pass deflection and six tackles. "And that's what it's always been about in the AFC North."

For the second straight week, the Steelers outgained their opponent on the ground by more than 130 yards.

Their 148 to 18 advantage over the New Orleans Saints last week secured a win in Paris. Their 200 rushing yards to the Browns' 34 on Sunday made a divisional opponent one dimensional, paving the way for eight sacks of Deshaun Watson a month after the Steelers notched just two on him.

Credit the Steelers' two-headed running attack of Warren and Rico Dowdle for part of that defensive success. Yes, Heyward gave the running backs flowers for what the defense did.

"They do a great job of being a one-two punch," Heyward said. "And so when they're able to sustain drives, that means [the defense] is on the sideline, and we can put our feet up."

Rodgers after 21-point win: 'Should've been a lot more points'

As rhythm eluded the Browns against the Steelers, AFC North counterparts Baltimore and Cincinnati were struggling, too.

The Baltimore Ravens entered Sunday with high hopes of avenging last year's blown game against the Buffalo Bills. Quarterback Lamar Jackson, for the first time in four games, was healthy enough to suit up.

Then, on the Ravens' first offensive snap, Jackson hit his throwing hand against Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau. A close-up shot from CBS' broadcast footage revealed what appeared to be swelling and an unnatural bend.

Later Sunday afternoon, the Ravens placed Jackson on injured reserve and announced he would undergo thumb surgery.

The Bengals escaped less scathed from a shootout against the Tennessee Titans . Most importantly for their playoff hopes, quarterback Joe Burrow suffered no injuries. But the Bengals still needed overtime to beat a one-win Titans team, Cincinnati's defense ceding a season-high 36 points. Burrow's 472 and six touchdowns from scrimmage (462, five passing) suggested his ceiling is as high as ever. The Bengals' four turnovers, with three Burrow interceptions and one Chase Brown fumble, called into question how reliable they are.

For a team that's already lost in a head-to-head with the Steelers, can the Bengals afford that?

The Ravens' and Bengals' weaknesses on display — Baltimore's more punishing, down to its emergency third quarterback after Tyler Huntley suffered a right toe injury — highlighted the division opportunity in the Browns' matchup against the Steelers.

Pittsburgh rose to the occasion. Cleveland stumbled.

"We certainly earned that," Browns head coach Todd Monken said of the loss. "We didn't start fast, turned the ball over a couple times early, then going three-and-out. Really never got the run game going. Couldn't stop the run early. Went three-and-out twice to start the second half, 10 penalties, didn't play with poise, however many sacks. So, didn't coach well enough, didn't play well enough.

"That's what's going to happen when you play a good team, a well-coached team, and you don't play your best. You don't give yourself a chance."

The Steelers leaned into their run game, parlaying 33 carries into 200 yards and all three of their touchdowns.

Warren led the pack with 143 yards and a score. Dowdle added 15 for 56, while tight end Pat Freiermuth scored on a 1-yard keeper.

"He's a bowling ball with teeth, man," outside linebacker T.J. Watt described Warren.

The Steelers appear to be finding their identity in their first year under head coach Mike McCarthy, who's reuniting with longtime Packers colleague and quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

Rodgers still makes a handful of key plays, including a third-quarter pass to tight end Darnell Washington that Washington took 58 yards. But even those plays most often feature heavy yards after the catch, Washington tacking on 44 to the 14 Rodgers sent the ball by air.

Mastering the line of scrimmage to set up his run game, Rodgers set up his teammates for success against the Browns. He felt the performance was "not very complete," particularly with two missed opportunities in the red zone, even as winning at the line of scrimmage powered Pittsburgh to victory.

"Defense played excellent, special teams did fine, but offense should've been a lot more points…" Rodgers said. "We'd like to play our best and still win. We also like to win. So we're 6-2 going into the bye, first in the division, so right where we want to be."

What do playoff predictors say about AFC North teams' chances?

At 4-4, the Ravens' chance at the division seems to be slipping. Healthy or nearly that, they may be the most talented team. But in a competitive division, with Jackson out at least four weeks and "potentially" the whole season per head coach Jesse Minter, Derrick Henry and co. seem unlikely to compensate.

The Ravens already return to prime time on Thursday to face the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars. Will Baltimore's fifth loss come then?

The Browns, right now, hold a 32% chance of making the playoffs, according to Next Gen Stats' playoff predictor model. It's a chance halfway through the season that perhaps exceeds some Browns fans' expectations entering Week 1 (and even moreso coming out of a miserable Week 1) and a benchmark that shouldn't surprise in light of the Browns' quiet rebuild. But it may disappoint fans taken in by Watson's fourth-quarter comebacks amassing more early wins than predicted.

This loss to Pittsburgh wasn't one Cleveland's playoff chances could comfortably afford. The Browns have more wins than every NFC East and NFC South team, but the AFC wild-card bid is still an uphill battle.

Then comes Cincinnati. At 5-2, the Bengals currently have an 86% chance to make the playoffs even as their division hopes are complicated by a 30-27 Week 3 loss to the Steelers. The teams rematch again in just two weeks, in Cincinnati. Pittsburgh will be more rested, coming off the bye. If the Steelers win, their path to the division crown will clarify still further.

"That game in two weeks is going to be really important," Rodgers said. "But yeah, right where we want to be."

Can the Steelers' frenetic defense and old-school offense power them deep into the playoffs? Despite their current hold on the division, Next Gen Stats — which factors strength of remaining opponents into its 10,000 simulations that create the formula — estimates a 75% chance to make the playoffs, strong if not as strong as Cincinnati's.

Pittsburgh was guarded in celebrating that its lopsided win could represent a step forward from four prior one-score wins. The Steelers' identity is starting to crystallize. But nine regular-season games remain.

"We can't take the foot off the gas one second here," Watt said. "Get our bodies back for bye week and come back blazing. …

"We still need to continue to go. Our identity is still being formed. A lot of football left."

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires Drew Rosenhaus in attempt to get wideout 'back to work and playing again in the NFL'
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk hasn't played in an NFL game since 2024.
articles.body:
It's been over two years since San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk played in an NFL game. After sustaining an ACL and MCL injury during the 2024 season, Aiyuk was initially placed on the PUP list ahead of 2025. But his relationship with the 49ers deteriorated, leading Aiyuk to not appear in a game despite still being under contract with the team.

Now the wideout is looking to change that. In an attempt to get back in the NFL, the 28-year-old Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, per multiple media reports. Rosenhaus told reporters he is tasked with "working on getting [Aiyuk] back to work and playing again in the NFL ."

Aiyuk was previously represented by agent Ryan Williams, but reportedly fired him last November. Aiyuk blamed Williams for the issues between the wideout and the 49ers.

In December, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list. He remains on there today.

Months after firing Williams, Aiyuk was vocal on social media, often expressing a desire to join the Washington Commanders. Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State for one season. That trade never materialized.

If Aiyuk is serious about returning to the NFL, his path forward is unclear. With his relationship with the 49ers ruined, the wideout would first likely need to establish his intent to play again. It's unclear, however, if Aiyuk would be willing to report to the team if the 49ers required it.

It's also unclear how much interest teams have in Aiyuk. While he proved to be immensely talented in 2022 and 2023, he hasn't played in an NFL game in two seasons and spent the past offseason torpedoing his chances of a return to the 49ers.

Given the injury questions and his personal baggage, Aiyuk might not draw much interest on the trade market.

While the 49ers could use help at wide receiver due to the team's various injuries, it doesn't appear the team is willing to welcome Aiyuk back. When asked about that possibility in September, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan simply replied "no" when the option was discussed .

Aiyuk is still under contract with the 49ers through the 2028 season. He signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the team in 2024, just months before his season-ending knee injury.

articles.title: Tom Brady's charity funding raised questions after another nonprofit provided nearly 98% of its money
articles.summary: Tom Brady built a reputation as one of the NFL's greatest quarterbacks, but his charitable work also attracted attention for an unexpected reason in 2017.
articles.body: Tom Brady built a reputation as one of the NFL's greatest quarterbacks, but his charitable work also attracted attention for an unexpected reason in 2017. An investigation into his nonprofit, Change the World, revealed that another organisation, Best Buddies, supplied almost all its funding. The arrangement was legal, but it raised questions about how Brady's charitable activities were financed and whether his work for one organisation was linked to donations made to his own foundation.Tom Brady's charity received nearly 98% of its funding from Best BuddiesA 2017 investigation by The Boston Globe, reported by Bob Hohler, brought attention to the financial relationship between Brady's Change the World charity and Best Buddies, an organisation founded by Anthony Shriver to improve the lives of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.Sports Illustrated legal analyst Michael McCann examined the arrangement in June 2017. His analysis highlighted a striking figure. Between approximately 2005 and 2015, Best Buddies provided nearly $2.3 million to Change the World, accounting for around 80% of the charity's funding. However, when Brady's initial contribution of $490,000 was excluded, the figure climbed to approximately 98%.The donations were publicly disclosed through nonprofit tax filings. Best Buddies also gave Change the World $500,000 in 2015, making it the largest donation recorded in that financial year. Its second-largest contribution was $200,000 to the Kevin Spacey Foundation.The arrangement prompted questions about whether Brady's fundraising work for Best Buddies was indirectly benefiting his own charitable interests. Rather than receiving personal compensation, the quarterback's charity received substantial financial support from the organisation.Tom Brady faced scrutiny over the relationship despite its charitable impactMcCann pointed out that donations between nonprofit organisations are legal and relatively common. He also noted that Brady did not take a salary from Change the World.However, the financial connection created an uncomfortable impression. Critics could question whether Brady's involvement with Best Buddies was entirely voluntary or whether its donations helped maintain his participation.McCann explained that Brady could have avoided the controversy by volunteering without accepting donations for his own foundation. Best Buddies could also have paid him directly for his fundraising and promotional work, although that would have created a different set of questions about charity expenses.Another point of discussion involved the organisations receiving money from Change the World. Its 2015 tax filing listed donations to Brady's former school, Junípero Serra High School, and the University of Michigan, where he played college football. Other recipients included Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Foundation Rwanda.Despite the concerns, McCann argued that the arrangement had delivered meaningful benefits. Best Buddies credited Brady with helping raise $46.5 million since 2001.His involvement brought attention and funding to people who needed support. Ultimately, the 2017 debate was not simply about where Brady's charity received its money. It was about transparency, public trust and whether a complicated financial arrangement could still produce a positive outcome.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Long before the Mahomes family became a regular topic of conversation among NFL fans, their Kansas City home was already making headlines for its impressive scale and luxury. In January 2024, Brittany Mahomes offered followers a rare look at one of its most personal spaces: her expansive walk-in closet. The glimpse revealed more than rows of shoes and designer bags. It offered a peek into the lifestyle Patrick Mahomes and his family had built after the quarterback secured a landmark contract with the Chiefs.Brittany Mahomes offers a glimpse inside her luxury closetBrittany shared the mirror selfie on Instagram Stories in January 2024, showing off a relaxed outfit while standing inside her spacious wardrobe. She wore a grey Vitality sweatshirt and matching joggers, priced at $82, along with a dark grey puffer vest worth $98. Knee-high Ugg boots completed the look.Her caption offered a glimpse into her everyday style. “I legit wear these sweet suits everyday …so glad I can mix them up now with a vest 🤣🙂,” she wrote.The outfit was casual, but the room behind her caught plenty of attention. Open shelves displayed an extensive collection of sneakers, heels and luxury handbags. Beige carpeting and a pink velvet chair added a softer touch to the space, making it feel more like a private dressing room than a standard closet.The reveal also showed how the couple's home reflected their success beyond the football field. Brittany, who was 28 at the time, had built a public profile of her own through business ventures, social media and her involvement with the Kansas City Current.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $8 million estate boasts impressive featuresThe closet was only one part of the couple's sprawling property. Patrick and Brittany began developing the estate in 2020 after purchasing an eight-acre plot reportedly worth $400,000. The decision came shortly after Patrick signed a 10-year, $450 million contract extension with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2020.Speaking about the project in Netflix's Quarterback, Patrick explained why he wanted to build a permanent home in the city.“I actually decided to get the land, to get ready to build that right, when I signed my contract here in Kansas City,” he explained.“I signed a 10-year extension … because I knew I wanted to be here,” he added.“So, right when I did that, I was like, ‘I’m gonna be here I might as well build the exact house I want.'”Completed in February 2023, the reported $8 million mansion featured an indoor basketball court, a modern gym and a private movie theatre. Outside, the property included a large swimming pool, hot tub, private pond, par-3 golf hole and a 50-yard football field.The estate also had a dedicated shower for the family's dogs, Steel and Silver. By January 2024, the couple were raising their two children, Sterling and Bronze, in the home. Their property had also become a gathering place for close friends, including Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift, who reportedly visited in November 2023.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens face potential franchise-shaking decision as trade speculation intensifies
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens could be approaching a crossroads with Lamar Jackson, and the latest injury setback has made an already uncertain situation even more
articles.body: The Baltimore Ravens could be approaching a crossroads with Lamar Jackson, and the latest injury setback has made an already uncertain situation even more complicated. The two-time NFL MVP suffered a thumb injury to his throwing hand during Sunday's crushing defeat to the Buffalo Bills. With surgery now required and his season potentially over, questions about his long-term future in Baltimore are growing louder. What once looked like another opportunity for the Ravens to build around their franchise quarterback could turn into a major offseason decision.Lamar Jackson's injury puts Ravens future under serious pressureBaltimore's 36-10 loss to Buffalo was damaging enough, but Jackson's injury made matters considerably worse. The quarterback hurt his throwing-hand thumb during the game and could miss the remainder of the season following surgery.The timing could hardly be worse for the Ravens. They currently sit at 4-4 and need stability at the quarterback position as they attempt to rescue their campaign.However, the bigger concern may be what happens after the season. ESPN's Dan Graziano believes a separation between Jackson and Baltimore is now a genuine possibility rather than an exaggerated prediction."If -- and this is still a big 'if' at this point -- this is a season-ending injury, then the Ravens and Jackson will head into a pivotal, potentially cataclysmic offseason," Graziano wrote in the piece. "Jackson's projected salary cap number for 2027 is $84.34M, which means the Ravens probably will want to extend him to knock down that number."That financial situation could force Baltimore into a difficult position. Jackson's projected cap figure of $84.34 million for 2027 would create a significant challenge for the franchise unless both sides reach an agreement on a new contract.Lamar Jackson contract dispute could open door to Ravens tradeThe contract situation is particularly complicated because Jackson has shown little interest in discussing another extension. That reluctance could leave the Ravens weighing a difficult choice if they cannot secure his future before the final year of his current deal.Graziano also explained why a potential trade cannot be dismissed."But Jackson isn't interested in talking an extension -- as was the case this past offseason -- so the Ravens will have a decision to make. And if they don't feel comfortable heading into the final year of Jackson's deal without an extension in place, we are going to hear legitimate talk of Jackson being traded. Jackson's contract also has a no-trade clause, which means he'd get to decide where he goes."The no-trade clause gives Jackson significant control over any potential move. Baltimore could explore a trade, but the quarterback would have a say in his destination.The Ravens had previously appeared keen to secure Jackson with another major extension. Now, his injury, contract position and the team's disappointing results have changed the conversation.A split is far from confirmed, and much will depend on Jackson's recovery and the discussions that follow. Still, Baltimore faces an offseason that could define the franchise for years. Its biggest question may no longer be how to build around Jackson, but whether he will remain its quarterback.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce-backed $200 million Six Flags faces two law firm investigations after fatal Goliath accident
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s connection to Six Flags has taken on a different dimension as the amusement park giant faces growing scrutiny following a fatal roller
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s connection to Six Flags has taken on a different dimension as the amusement park giant faces growing scrutiny following a fatal roller coaster accident. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end, who serves as a Six Flags ambassador and investor, is associated with a brand now dealing with serious questions about ride safety and maintenance. The October 12 tragedy at Six Flags Over Georgia claimed the life of a 42-year-old guest and left four other riders injured. With new eyewitness accounts emerging and law firms examining the company, the incident has placed Six Flags under an uncomfortable spotlight.Travis Kelce’s Six Flags connection faces an unexpected challengeKelce's involvement with Six Flags gives the unfolding situation an added layer of public interest. His association with the entertainment company connects one of the NFL's biggest stars to a business facing questions about its safety standards and operations.The tragedy involved Goliath, one of the park's major roller coaster attractions. Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, from Atlanta, died after being thrown from the ride. Four other passengers, all minors, sustained non-life-threatening injuries.Investigators have yet to establish what caused the fatal fall. However, accounts from other visitors have raised concerns about possible restraint problems before the accident.One mother told The Associated Press that her children experienced trouble with a restraint roughly an hour before the incident. Another account shared by Kariem's family suggested that he appeared to lose consciousness before his restraint came loose.These accounts remain unverified, and authorities have not confirmed a mechanical failure.The questions surrounding Goliath have also drawn attention to the company's wider safety practices. Six Flags temporarily closed nine additional roller coasters across six parks as a precaution after the tragedy.Six Flags investigation raises fresh questions about roller coaster safetyThe investigation has now expanded beyond the circumstances of the accident. Two shareholder-rights law firms, Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP and Robbins LLP, have announced separate investigations into Six Flags Entertainment Corporation.Bleichmar Fonti & Auld is examining whether the company made misleading statements to investors about safety, maintenance and ride reliability. The firm also reported that Six Flags shares dropped approximately 14.4% on October 13 following news of the fatality and coaster closures.Meanwhile, Six Flags has announced an independent safety review covering inspection procedures, preventive maintenance, employee training, operating practices and documentation.The company has also confirmed that Goliath, Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure and Raging Bull at Six Flags Great America will receive additional seat belts.Meanwhile, Georgia authorities continue examining maintenance records, ride equipment and operational procedures. A March 2026 inspection of Goliath recorded no violations, although a maintenance note mentioned bushings that required replacement. Six Flags sources later said those components had been replaced.For Kelce, whose ambassador and investor relationship ties him to the brand, the developing investigation presents an uncomfortable backdrop. However, there is no indication that he had any involvement in the ride's operations or the incident.Until investigators establish what happened, Goliath remains closed with no confirmed reopening date. The findings could have important consequences for Six Flags and its efforts to maintain public confidence in its attractions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love Has 'New' Injury, Latest Updates on Cardinals RB's Ankle After Exiting vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Jeremiyah Love's difficult rookie season took another turn on Sunday.
articles.body:
Jeremiyah Love's difficult rookie season took another turn on Sunday.

According to Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur, Love suffered a new ankle injury during the 33-30 overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys.

"It just stinks for him," LaFleur told reporters. "He wants to be out there helping his teammates. This guy loves ball. He just wants to contribute. He's such a team guy, such a coachable guy, he's such a likable guy. He just wants to be out there helping his guys. For him, going through what he's going through, it's adversity for sure, but he's gonna be stronger because of this."

Love, 21, has already dealt with ankle issues in both the preseason and during the regular season, with this latest issue affecting a different part of the ankle than his previous ailments.

Those injuries have hampered what was a much-anticipated rookie season from the No. 3 overall pick at the 2026 NFL draft. In six games Love has rushed for just 268 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 catches for 36 yards and another score.

Many fans—and fantasy football enthusiasts—expected Love to hit the ground running as Arizona's featured back, but that hasn't materialized. Instead he's operated in more of a platoon with Tyler Allgeier, and Sunday was his first game back after a two-game absence due to his ongoing ankle issues.

"I am myself when I got my ankles," Love told reporters last week. "I feel like, as a running back or as a receiver, a lot of the moves that we do with our ankles and knees and stuff like that, I like to come to complete stops. It impacted me quite a bit. ... I just want to go out there and be myself. I feel like the past few games, for really the whole season, I haven't really been able to go out there and just feel like myself. I just feel like I just can't go or I couldn't go out there and just do what I wanted to."

This latest ankle injury seems like a setback in that regard.

articles.title: Giants' John Harbaugh Defends Calling Titans Owner About Jeffery Simmons Trade amid Criticism
articles.summary: The New York Giants sit atop the NFC East as the trade deadline approaches, and they attempted to make a move for one of the biggest stars on the trade market.
articles.body:
The New York Giants sit atop the NFC East as the trade deadline approaches, and they attempted to make a move for one of the biggest stars on the trade market.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed to reporters Monday that he reached out to Tennessee Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk directly to inquire about defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who was later traded to the Chicago Bears.

"I did, I did. I left a message," he said. "...Because you turn over every stone. You know, gonna try everything. I mean, I just, I'll put it out there, man, we're open for any call. Anybody wants to call us or call anybody. Call."

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported last week that Harbaugh had called Strunk about Simmons. It's standard to do business through a general manager rather than through an owner directly.

Harbaugh isn't concerned about breaking any unwritten rules.

"We're not like — we're not part of any secret society oath that says you can only talk to somebody. We're not in that," he said. "We didn't get memoed on that. We're not in that agreement. So like I said, anybody can call us. We won't be adhering to that particular agreement."

Ultimately, Harbaugh's direct effort to land Simmons didn't work out. The Bears sent a pair of first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to Tennessee in return for Simmons and a fifth-round pick.

articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have lost six straight games, but head coach Nick Sirianni isn't planning on making any drastic changes.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have lost six straight games, but head coach Nick Sirianni isn't planning on making any drastic changes.

Sirianni said he won't relieve offensive coordinator Sean Mannion of his duties, and Tanner McKee will remain the starting quarterback.

"I'm not making any changes there," Sirianni told reporters when asked about his coaching staff. "It is on all of us to figure out how to get things going in the right direction. Obviously, right now they're not. But again, this is the ultimate team game and we're in the problem-solving business. Right now, we have to find answers to help us get going offensively. Again, that brunt falls on myself, that falls on Sean, and we're going to do everything we can to get ourselves out of this."

The Eagles haven't won since Week 2 against the Tennessee Titans and are without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the year because of blood clots.

In a 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday, McKee had 212 yards and an interception on 23-of-34 passing. The 2023 sixth-round pick has thrown for 638 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in three games.

"Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there," Sirianni said. "Again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme, that could be within how our schedule is, practice plays. Everything's on the table for us in that aspect. But right now, this is where we are and we're trying to find solutions there. We're looking at everything as far as what we can do differently as coaches."

Behind McKee is Joe Milton, whom the Eagles signed off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad. Milton, a sixth-round pick in 2024, threw for 183 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions while backing up Dak Prescott last year.

Philadelphia also has rookie Cole Payton available. The fifth-round pick has not yet appeared in a game for the Eagles.

Mannion retired from the NFL in 2023 and spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Green Bay Packers, first as an offensive assistant and then as the quarterbacks coach. The Eagles gave him his first offensive coordinator job this year, and it hasn't gone well so far.

Philadelphia ranks last in yards per game (265.3) and 30th in points per game (17.1).

But Mannion has had plenty of challenges to overcome, mainly injuries, and it seems Sirianni wants to see things through before giving up on him.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill faces fresh uncertainty over his future as insider questions the need for a Kansas City Chiefs reunion
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has found his career in a mess as he continues to remain a free agent even though it has been two
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has found his career in a mess as he continues to remain a free agent even though it has been two months since the new season started. The last time Tyreek Hill was spotted on the field was last September when his run on the field ended early as he sustained brutal injuries. While there have been rumors of a potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs, ESPN’s Dan Graziano has reflected on it.NFL insider weighs in on Tyreek Hill’s potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs amid a slow recoveryA few hours ago, ESPN’s Dan Graziano weighed in on how it could be difficult for Tyreek Hill to have a potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs.ESPN’s Dan Graziano noted in a recent report, “They just aren't playing to their potential. Guys like that are supposed to be the solutions."ESPN’s Dan Graziano also compared the Denver Broncos’ Jaylen Waddle to Tyreek Hill as he noted, "I expect both of these teams to work to improve their offenses ahead of next week's trade deadline, which could mean adding at wide receiver…”ESPN’s Dan Graziano added, “But that wouldn't be necessary if the wide receivers they already spent so much to get would play better. articles.title: Coach Matt LaFleur Says Packers Anticipate Keeping Josh Jacobs on Their Roster
articles.summary: Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur says the Packers plan to keep Josh Jacobs on their roster following the news of previous allegations against the running back, who has pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.
articles.body:
Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur says the Packers plan to keep Josh Jacobs on their roster following the news of previous allegations against the running back, who has pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.

"We're going to allow the NFL to do its process, but I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward," LaFleur said Monday. "That's really all I have to speak on."

LaFleur was asked why the Packers weren't cutting ties with Jacobs.

"Because we're just going to let everything kind of play out and obviously go from there," he replied.

Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He was arrested May 26 after his then-girlfriend said he had thrown her to the ground three days earlier.

In response to a public records request, the Hobart-Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department released records from their investigation Friday night that included the accounts of three other women who reported similar incidents from years before.

After spending the first six games of the season on the commissioner's exempt list, which prevented him from playing or practicing, Jacobs returned to play in the Packers' last two games. The NFL has said its investigation into Jacobs is ongoing, which means he still could be subject to more discipline from the league.

Lawyers representing Jacobs said he has a "substantial body of tangible evidence" disputing the allegations that surfaced in Friday's records release.

"Josh took responsibility for what happened in May," David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III said Sunday in a statement. "He entered into an agreement with prosecutors for two misdemeanors, and he is meeting the court's requirements.

"The three accounts are old, are hearsay, and easily disproven, yet released to the media by police without any investigation to determine whether they were accurate or contradicted by evidence. Josh is answering them in detail because of the character assassination that is occurring, unfairly threatening his career."

Jacobs' lawyers said that one of the three women made a claim to the NFL, which reviewed it and decided no action was warranted. They said Jacobs "has kept evidence that supports his accounts and the NFL's decision."

The NFL declined comment Sunday on the lawyers' statement. After Hobart-Lawrence police released the records that detailed the accounts from the other women, NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy had said Saturday that the league would review these allegations as part of its investigation.

After charges were initially filed against Jacobs, LaFleur said on Sept. 1 that "I believe him and I trust him" and added that "I'm going to do that until proven otherwise." When Jacobs came off the commissioner's exempt list and started practicing with the Packers again two weeks ago, LaFleur said that "I think people learn from their mistakes and I think he's extremely remorseful and I do believe that he's a good person."

LaFleur was asked Monday about his support for Jacobs and whether anything had changed in that regard.

"I'm not going to get into that up here right now," LaFleur said. "We'll just let the process play out."

Jacobs' arrest followed a May 23 incident in which police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, a woman told them Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

Since returning to the Packers, Jacobs has 32 carries for 75 yards and a touchdown plus 11 catches for 68 yards and two more scores.

Jacobs scored two touchdowns in a 27-19 victory over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday and celebrated the first of those scores by briefly putting his hands together behind his back. Jacobs said after the game that he was paying homage to a gospel song titled "Break Every Chain," but he was criticized on social media by people who believed he was simulating getting handcuffed.

"That's something that he and I talked about," LaFleur said. "I know he had his explanation, and I wasn't even aware of what happened until I saw the tape. But we had a conversation about that, and I'm going to keep the conversation between him and I, and you know, we're going to move forward."

articles.title: NFL Playoff Bracket Scenarios 2026-27 Week 9 After Caleb Williams, Bears Upset Seahawks on MNF
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears delivered a statement on the road with a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears delivered a statement on the road with a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night.

The Bears won't end the night in first place in the division or conference, but they showcased just how dangerous of a team they can be against the reigning Super Bowl champion.

Caleb Williams and Co. will head into Week 9 with a half-game deficit beneath the Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North.

Seattle dropped down to .500 with the defeat. It sits on the outside of the NFC wild-card race right now, but it is only one game behind the Green Bay Packers for the No. 7 seed.

Chicago is one of four NFC North teams in a playoff position at the end of Week 8.

There's a real chance the Bears get into the playoff field alongside the Minnesota Vikings, Detroit Lions and Green Bay Packers given the lack of competitiveness in the NFC East and South.

The 6-2 Bears have the chance to feast on the NFC North in their next two games. They host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next Sunday night and then welcome the New Orleans Saints in Week 11 off the bye.

Chicago has four games left against its divisional foes, so there's plenty of time for it to get in front of the competition and make a run for the No. 1 seed.

As for Seattle, it needs to find a way to rebound in the next two weeks against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders. Two wins in those games would allow the Seahawks to carry some confidence into the bye and rest up for the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12.

The Seahawks play four games against the NFC East and South after their Week 11 bye. The other three contests in the closing stretch come against the 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams.

The reigning Super Bowl champion isn't in a good spot now, but the favorable schedule should allow the Seahawks to get into the top seven by mid December.

Ten teams have a realistic chance to make the AFC postseason based on record.

You could argue, though, the Baltimore Ravens with all of their quarterback injury issues are more on the outside looking in than the Las Vegas Raiders and Cleveland Browns.

All three teams in the AFC wild-card positions have five victories, as do the Browns in eighth. The four division leaders sit with five or six wins, so any set of results in any given week could significantly alter the AFC standings.

Baltimore faces a tough Thursday night home clash with Jacksonville. A loss in that game could put the Ravens in a tough spot when it comes to their playoff chances.

A majority of the playoff contenders in the AFC play out-of-conference games in Week 9, a slate headlined by the Buffalo Bills' Monday night showdown with the Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Caleb Williams, Bears Beat Seahawks, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Darnold, JSN, Swift, More
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears look like Super Bowl contenders.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears look like Super Bowl contenders.

Chicago defeated the reigning-champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in Monday's NFC showdown at Lumen Field to improve to 6-2 overall with its third straight win. Caleb Williams was in full control of the offense, while D'Andre Swift scored three touchdowns as the Bears offense set the tone.

As for Sam Darnold and Seattle, it fell to 4-4 on the season and just 2-4 in its last six. The playoffs are far from a guarantee at this point and will require better play that what was on display Monday.

The lead up to this highly anticipated showdown only added more hype, as the Bears traded for defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons and the Seahawks traded for offensive lineman Quenton Nelson. They battled each other for years in the AFC South, and the moves were a further sign both of these teams are all in on chasing the Lombardi Trophy.

It was a good-on-good Monday night matchup and a chance to make a statement, and Chicago made the opening one when Williams directed a 17-play, 80-yard drive that included a fourth-down conversion, some tight-window throws and a touchdown strike to Luther Burden III for the game's first points.

The visitors eventually built a double-digit lead in the second quarter and had plenty of momentum after Simmons notched his first sack for his new team, but Smith-Njigba is also inevitable.

Seattle's star receiver broke free shortly before the half for a massive 43-yard touchdown that swung the momentum his team's way despite a four-point deficit at intermission.

The Seahawks defense isn't accustomed to giving up long, time-consuming drives, but they gave up another one in the third quarter when Williams marched the Bears 69 yards on 10 plays. Swift finished the drive of more than six minutes with a touchdown run, which put Chicago back up double digits.

As if that wasn't troubling enough for Seattle, Austin Booker blocked a field goal on the ensuing possession to maintain the two-score advantage early in the fourth quarter.

Just when it seemed like Chicago was going to put it away, Seattle's defense made a play like it has all year. It forced a Colston Loveland fumble, which the offense parlayed into a touchdown pass from Darnold to Cooper Kupp and a two-point conversion to cut the deficit to three.

That put all the pressure on the Bears to respond on the road.

Chicago answered with Swift's second touchdown of the game, although the biggest play of the drive was a 39-yard gain by Kalif Raymond for a key third-down conversion.

From there, James Lynch picked off a batted ball to set up Swift's third touchdown and create all the breathing room the visitors needed.

The Bears now return home for a matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, while the Seahawks will look to bounce back when they host the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 9: Broncos are 6-2 but need to improve, perhaps with some pre-deadline trades
articles.summary: Denver is winning close games at an incredible rate, but it may not be able to count on that continuing without some trade additions.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Denver Broncos went 14-3 last season with an inordinate amount of wins in close games. Everyone said that was unsustainable and they were due for regression.

This season, the Broncos are 6-2 with an inordinate amount of wins in close games. Take that, regression police.

Somehow, the Broncos are again pulling off what should be impossible. On Sunday they came back from a 24-13 deficit in the fourth quarter to beat the Kansas City Chiefs , who have had their own fortunate run in close games. It was the Broncos' 15th straight win in games decided by eight points or less, tying the 2008-09 Indianapolis Colts for the NFL record, according to ESPN Insights .

One of two things has to be true: The Broncos are incredibly lucky in games that shouldn't be far off a 50-50 proposition and that's bound to flip, or they have some skill in winning close games that nobody else has possessed aside from Peyton Manning's Colts more than 15 years ago. Regardless of how they've gotten to their impressive record, Denver has overtaken Kansas City for the best chance to win the AFC West at 56.4%, according to DVOA .

"I think honestly, to answer that, I think it has to come from, well, we did it before," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said about winning close games, according to the team's transcripts. "Then there's a belief that can get stronger and then there's experience and then you're seasoned a little, but we still have a lot of things to fix. I honestly think that's where I believe it comes from."

If the Broncos decide they are on a heater in which the coin is repeatedly flipping on their side for a statistically improbable reason, they have some work to do before the trade deadline on Nov. 10. The offense, which has been inconsistent all season and was catching boos from the home crowd Sunday after three straight three-and-outs to start the second half, should be the focus.

Denver is just 30th in yards gained this season. A play-calling change from offensive coordinator Davis Webb to Payton hasn't helped much. The Broncos aren't getting a quarterback to replace Bo Nix but practically every other position group could be a candidate for an upgrade. The defense is good enough for a long playoff run, as it was last season. The variable is the offense.

Or maybe it just doesn't matter. The Broncos have beaten the odds for two seasons. They're 20-5 since the start of the 2025 season and 16 of those wins have been by eight points or less. They continue to laugh at the regression proclamations.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 8 of the NFL season, looking at the biggest need for each team before the trade deadline:

32 Los Angeles Chargers (0-7, Last week: 32)

The Chargers' season is lost, so the obvious move is to trade veterans who can help elsewhere. Mack is clearly at the top of that list. He has started all seven games, has three sacks and can add immediate legitimacy to a defense from the edge. He's a likely future Hall of Famer and while he isn't quite the same player at age 35, he's still an asset. He's also no stranger to being traded, having been dealt from the Raiders to the Bears and then the Bears to the Chargers earlier in his career.

"You've got to be where your feet are man, ultimately," Mack said, via Eric Williams of Fox Sports . "That can be the most difficult thing when you're dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all time. That's kind of been my thing in years past."

Biggest need: Get value for Jonathan Taylor

The way the Colts gave up on Sunday, they probably should have made Taylor inactive. Everyone knows they're going to try to trade him after shipping off guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. The Colts need to restock their draft picks after a regrettable trade that sent two first-round picks, including their 2027 first, to the Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner. And, presumably, they feel some obligation to find a good home for Taylor, who has been a tremendous player for them through the years.

There will be plenty of teams, perhaps the Giants, Broncos, Packers and Vikings among them, talking about trading for Taylor, so the Colts should get a good return.

"And you know that day always comes for many players,'' Taylor said about the possibility of being traded last week, via Fox 59 . "Whether you like it or not, the day may come. You may get lucky enough to stay somewhere forever, but you understand the business of it.

Others, like defensive tackle Grover Stewart and receiver Josh Downs, could be traded too. It's going to be a rough rest of the season for Indianapolis.

Biggest need: Hang onto Garrett Wilson and others

The Jets are in a great spot. If the NFL Draft was today, they'd have the fourth pick from the Colts (Sauce Gardner trade), their own pick at No. 6 and the 10th pick from the Cowboys (Quinnen Williams trade). That would be historic.

Unlike last season, when the Jets were willing to deal young players for a stockpile of picks, the right move seems to be holding onto some foundational pieces. The one that would generate a ton of interest is Wilson, who has mostly been wasted away with the Jets. But he's 26 years old, signed through 2030, and is a legitimate No. 1 receiver. Perhaps there's a minor move to be made, like trading cornerback Nahshon Wright, but the Jets already did their trading work with the 2027 draft in mind and now it's time to stand pat.

Biggest need: Trade Moro Ojomo, maybe Saquon Barkley, and many others

Howie Roseman might be the busiest general manager with the trade deadline coming up. He usually does well in trades — we'll ignore that he traded two third-round picks for two tackles and zero sacks from Jonathan Greenard so far this season — and he has plenty of assets to move.

Barkley is the most interesting figure, even as the team reportedly won't move him . A trade would make too much sense for the Eagles to not entertain any inquiries. Any team that gets him would be gambling because Barkley has been injured most of the season and his numbers are way down since his magical (and high usage) 2024 season. Multiple teams are in need of a playmaking running back. It'll be interesting to see if the Eagles' stance on Barkley changes in the next week. The bigger piece might be Ojomo, a good defensive tackle who is about to be a free agent. The Eagles could keep him and try to re-sign him, but they have a lot of money invested at defensive tackle. Tight end Dallas Goedert, edge rusher Nolan Smith and cornerback Riq Woolen are others who should be available for the right price.

It would be surprising if the Eagles aren't very active.

Biggest need: Find draft picks for some aging vets

Once the Titans traded defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, it was a sign that any veteran was available. And the Titans have a few who don't fit in the long-term plans.

Given the hot streak running back Tony Pollard has been on, he has emerged as perhaps the most intriguing piece. Receiver Calvin Ridley is buried on the depth chart but some team could take a shot on him for a third-day draft pick. Safety Amani Hooker, who is 28 years old, has been tremendous. Edge rusher Jermaine Johnson II, in the final year of his deal, could be moved too. The Titans could have a ton of extra draft picks by the time the deadline is done.

Biggest need: Figure out what to do with Zach Sieler

Sieler has been a productive defensive tackle for many years, but he's also 31 years old. Still, the Dolphins haven't entertained trade talks for him, according to SI.com . Miami is in full rebuild mode and while Sieler helps the Dolphins now, a 1-6 team should be looking for the future, and trading a 31-year-old defensive lineman who still would have plenty of trade value makes sense. We'll see what the Dolphins do.

Trading offensive tackle Austin Jackson has also been speculated, and teams are always looking for line help. The stripped-down Dolphins roster doesn't have a lot of attractive veteran trade candidates, which makes the decision on Sieler that much more important.

Biggest need: Figuring out if they're buyers or sellers

A 2-5, last-place team should not be thinking about buying. But most teams don't have the luxury of playing in the NFC South, where 2-5 is just a game out of first place. There are pieces the Saints could trade and easily absorb the loss, like running back Kendre Miller and safety Justin Reid. Perhaps that's a way to straddle the line of competing for a division title and thinking toward the future. The Saints also should be getting running back Travis Etienne Jr. and rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson back from injuries as soon as this week, so that will feel like a pair of deadline acquisitions.

The Saints are very much in the race in a bad division. They're also early in a rebuild and their record indicates they're still in need of draft picks and young talent. That makes it a challenge to figure out what to do before the deadline.

Biggest need: Adding to the defense, maybe

At some point the Cowboys need to have an honest conversation about themselves, which seems impossible after team owner Jerry Jones proclaimed everyone is letting head coach Brian Schottenheimer down. Jones has talked about making big trades, and already made one in-season for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. A putrid defense that let Gardner Minshew tear it apart in the fourth quarter and overtime on Sunday needs a lot of help. But, is a team that has losses at home to a Buccaneers team led by an undrafted rookie quarterback and to a Cardinals team that came back from a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter really a defensive piece away from contending for a Super Bowl? Probably not.

It puts the Cowboys in a weird place. They're not out of the NFC East race because the division isn't good . They're also not very good themselves. It's not even outlandish for the Cowboys to look in the mirror after that hideous loss to the Cardinals and admit they should be sellers. That would require self-awareness, which isn't abundant in Dallas.

Biggest need: Making a move on two defensive standouts

The Cardinals should be feeling good about themselves after a win at Dallas, their third upset road win of the season. They should also be realistic. The Cardinals aren't going to compete for a playoff spot. The progress is great but it's still a rebuild. That makes them an interesting seller.

The top trade candidate is probably edge rusher Josh Sweat, who came over from the Eagles after helping Philadelphia win a Super Bowl and hasn't had a ton of impact on a non-contending team. There's also a question about safety Budda Baker, one of Arizona's best players but is 30 years old and signed through only 2027. Both of those players could fetch valuable draft picks in a deal.

There's also question now if quarterback Jacoby Brissett could move; he was benched on Sunday and replaced by Gardner Minshew, who has been named the starter for Week 9 vs. the Seahawks . Minshew and Carson Beck are higher priorities now. But the biggest key is finding the best return for Sweat and perhaps Baker.

23. Washington Commanders (2-4-1, LW: 24)

Like everyone else in the NFC South and NFC East, other than the Eagles, the Commanders should feel like they have a shot to be division champions. The Commanders are flawed, without question, but sit just two games behind the Giants in the division. It's not like New York is a lock to run away with it.

The biggest problem for the Commanders is the loss of receiver Terry McLaurin for the season. It leaves them thin at receiver, and the good news is there are a lot of veterans available at the deadline at various price points. The Commanders should be interested. They also should be interested in improving a secondary that ranks 27th in passing yards allowed.

The biggest question for the Ravens is this: Can Lamar Jackson return for the playoffs from a thumb injury suffered on Sunday? If the answer is yes, it's not outrageous for a team with a .500 record to see what it can do to keep playoff hopes alive until Jackson can come back. The problem is that it's hard to find any quarterback who can save a season (contrary to everything you see before the trade deadline, NFL teams aren't excited to trade away their backup quarterback). Still, the Ravens have to look. As much as the Ravens like Tyler Huntley, he's not the answer, especially now that he's dealing with a toe injury. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is very, very unlikely to keep the Ravens in playoff contention.

However, if Jackson is done for the rest of the season with no hope for the playoffs, the Ravens probably have to turn the page and sell. It would hurt, but it would kickstart what could be a huge offseason of change in Baltimore . Because without Jackson, the Ravens' ranking of No. 22 here might be generous.

The Falcons are in a weird space. They're tied with the Buccaneers for second place in the NFC South, a half game behind the Panthers (3-4). They also are one of the most inconsistent teams in the NFL. They followed up beating the previously undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a single pass .

Atlanta is wildly inconsistent on offense, and that's why adding a receiver to go alongside Drake London makes sense. But the offense should be good enough, when it's not playing in a rainstorm like Sunday, to contend in the division. The defense needs help. And it could use it at almost every position aside from off-ball linebacker and safety. It's weird for a 3-5 team to clearly be buyers, but that's the 2026 NFC South.

A sub-.500 team that just fired its defensive coordinator also doesn't profile as a buyer, but the Panthers are in the 2026 NFC South. Their defense needs help, and firing Ejiro Evero doesn't solve all the problems. Being without cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, who are both on injured reserve, is tough to overcome. Getting some help there would be wise. A pass rusher would be nice too, considering Jaelan Phillips has been injured and isn't living up to his $120 million contract signed in the offseason.

It's not like the offense doesn't need help too, particularly the offensive line's depth because of injuries. Coming off an NFC South title and striving for another, the Panthers will be looking around before the deadline. There are a few areas that could use help.

The Texans made a big and questionable move in the offseason, trading fourth- and seventh-round draft picks, along with offensive lineman Juice Scruggs, to the Lions for running back David Montgomery. Scruggs has been more valuable this season than Montgomery, who has averaged 2.7 yards per carry and missed two games with injury. Woody Marks hasn't been much better. Houston has no running game and it's a big reason it is 2-5.

Do the Texans possibly trade for another running back? Do they trade for anyone at all? It's hard to give up the idea that Houston can still get back in the playoff race. It's a talented but underachieving team. But the Texans still have a 33.8% shot to make the playoffs, via DVOA , and can theoretically be a dangerous playoff opponent. Is that enough to ship off more picks, especially if it's for another running back?

Biggest need: Not being myopic about trading picks

A team two games under .500 now has a 57.4% chance to host a playoff game as a division winner, according to DVOA . The NFC South, everyone!

The Buccaneers might have been sellers two weeks ago, with veterans like receiver Chris Godwin Jr. and defensive end YaYa Diaby available, but that mentality likely changes after decisive wins over the Panthers and Falcons. Still, this is a 3-5 team and advanced metrics say the Bucs are pretty good as is (they rank a surprising fifth in DVOA). Tampa doesn't have a pressing need, though defensive help is always welcomed. The Buccaneers can stand pat, keep their picks and still be the favorite in the NFC South while not giving away any valuable picks for the future.

Biggest need: Remembering the long-term plan

It's hard for a franchise that hasn't had much success over the past few decades to have a level head over a solid start to the season. At 4-4, the Raiders can talk themselves into being playoff contenders. That makes it hard to be a seller. It would be an even harder thing to explain to longtime fans who are dying for a taste of success or a new fan base in Las Vegas that hasn't fully embraced the Raiders yet.

Realistically, the Raiders probably should be closer to sellers than they are to buyers. Could they find out if a team is willing to pay a heavy premium for Maxx Crosby like the Ravens (almost) did in March? It's not like the Ravens' concerns about Crosby's knee over the long term have vanished. However, ESPN reported the Raiders have no plans to trade Crosby. It also seems very unlikely the Raiders trade Kirk Cousins, but what if a desperate team is willing to overpay for a viable quarterback who already has 19 touchdown passes? Wouldn't they have to listen? It's not like Cousins is the future and they'll want to get Fernando Mendoza some valuable reps before the end of the season even if Cousins stays aboard. It seems foolish to be buyers when they're well behind the Broncos and Chiefs in the AFC West. And the big picture says that they should be quietly gauging the market on Crosby, Cousins and any others without long-term value, even if that would be unpopular to many Raiders fans.

Like the Raiders, it's fun for a team that has had almost no success to start 5-2. An uncompetitive loss to the Steelers on Sunday should put the Browns in a more realistic mindset. They can't keep living off last-minute wins, and their poor quarterback situation makes their level of success unsustainable. The five wins have already put the Browns in a bad spot to find a quarterback solution in 2027, but that's a conversation for next offseason.

The Browns can still be partial sellers without hurting their playoff hopes for this season. Receiver Jerry Jeudy is tradable and there are plenty of teams that could use him. Offensive tackle Dawand Jones, a backup who could provide depth elsewhere, can also be available. But with a promising young core, the Browns have to be careful to not get ahead of themselves despite a 5-3 record.

The Giants landing a running back is one of the easiest predictions of the trade deadline. They have plenty of injuries at the position, seem lukewarm at best on Cam Skattebo, but have a great chance to win a bad division.

How much do the Giants want to pay for a running back? Jonathan Taylor is the dream, but he won't be cheap. Perhaps Tony Pollard will be more reasonable, though he has played very well lately and that could increase the price.

The Giants will be looking at every possibility to help at running back, which could push them closer to a division title.

The Packers are one of a few teams in need of a running back and it's a different situation than the rest. If Josh Jacobs was a sure thing the rest of the season, the Packers might concentrate on more offensive line help or simply hold tight, knowing Micah Parsons is on the way soon.

But Jacobs' legal situation took a turn over the weekend after more allegations of abuse were reported. He denied wrongdoing, but the NFL can revisit the case. We have seen how poor the Packers' running game was without Jacobs. Green Bay doesn't want to be stuck again in that situation if Jacobs faces further punishment. Adding a viable starter would allow the Packers to move on from Jacobs entirely.

Biggest need: Receiver or cornerback, but probably nothing

A team that has among the oldest rosters in the NFL and is 6-2 before the deadline might generally be a big buyer to make a push with an aging team. Yet, it doesn't seem like there's one move that can put the Steelers on the same level as some of the NFL's elite teams.

Another receiver would be nice, but there's a lot of money tied up in DK Metcalf, and someone like Josh Downs would be redundant with the skill set of intriguing rookie Germie Bernard. Perhaps adding Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr. would make sense. Cornerback could help after trading away Joey Porter Jr., but the Steelers have been good at that position without him. An old team trading away valuable picks seems bad for the future. And a 6-2 team trading someone like edge rusher Alex Highsmith seems like the wrong move too. We might see Pittsburgh make a minor move or two but little else.

The Rams have already invested heavily into the 2026 roster, so what's the big deal in sending off more draft picks? For now, the Rams are playing coy, saying that players they could get back from injury, like Myles Garrett and Davante Adams, would serve as their deadline additions.

"Based on our situation, I mean the good thing for us is, what you look at is hopefully some of those trades will be guys getting back from injury that haven't played for us," head coach Sean McVay said, via the Los Angeles Times . "That's kind of the way we look at it."

Yet, it's hard to believe that because of the Rams' history. And while the idea of getting Adams back from a major hamstring injury is good in theory, he'll turn 34 on Dec. 24 and it's not a guarantee he returns to his normal level. The Rams are very thin at receiver behind Puka Nacua while Adams heals, and it's not like Nacua doesn't have a long injury history. Maybe the Rams stay put, but it wouldn't be a surprise if they talk themselves into a deal. Grabbing an exciting receiver might give the sluggish Rams a spark.

The Dolphins don't have a good pass rush but they still pressured Drake Maye often in Week 8. Maye overcame that with a strong second half to lead the Patriots to a win, but it's not like the line issues are going away. Guards Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker are on injured reserve. Getting a guard to help makes a lot of sense.

The Patriots have also had some trade speculation on the selling side. Cornerback Carlton Davis III could be dealt, according to Albert Breer of SI.com . Davis returned from a neck injury for Week 8 and played 96.9% of the defensive snaps, but it's possible the Patriots want to trade him for extra draft capital, which they could use to improve at guard.

Biggest need: Some help for Jaxon Smith-Njigba

It's surprising to see Smith-Njigba at a 36.3% target share entering Monday night's game, because it's rare for a receiver to get that many of a team's targets. But then you look around Seattle's offense and realize there's no other viable option. Smith-Njigba has 985 yards this season and Cooper Kupp is second on the team at 206.

The Seahawks decided to address their run game by adding guard Quenton Nelson instead of one of the name-brand running backs who might be available. Maybe that's their only big move. But for an offense that has been uneven most of the season, another receiving threat would help. It would help take pressure off turnover-prone Sam Darnold.

The idea that the Broncos could make a big move for Jonathan Taylor is dubious only because Sean Payton's history of using committees at running back without a standout workhorse. And the team has to be intrigued by rookie Jonah Coleman, who has played well and came up with two big plays to give Denver the lead in a huge win over the Chiefs on Sunday.

Perhaps Taylor or another big-time back could solve some issues on the offense. Or maybe it's a receiver or a tight end, after the Evan Engram signing in 2025 has been a dud. Even some depth on the offensive line isn't a bad idea. The Broncos are set on defense, so their focus can be how to add an impact piece to an inconsistent offense.

Biggest need: Defense, particularly at cornerback

The Lions' fan base wasn't happy when the Cowboys overpaid to get cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade. They know that cornerback is an issue and it seems hard to believe the deadline will pass without Detroit doing something at the position.

Yet, there are other issues on a defense that has struggled most of the season, though it has allowed just 32 points the last two games. While the human element of linebacker Jack Campbell's neck injury is overwhelming, and his recovery is the biggest part of that story , there is a football side to it as well. Detroit will presumably be without one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL indefinitely. While the team's thoughts are primarily on their young star's health, the Lions also have to deal with the reality of perhaps adding a linebacker before the deadline.

Biggest need: Receiver, but don't forget about offensive line

This is no surprise: The Chiefs still need help at receiver. Their offense has been built around Kenneth Walker III to good results, but it's an incomplete unit. Rashee Rice is productive but not a dominant No. 1, Xavier Worthy hasn't broken out and there's not much else to speak of. Among the Chiefs' wideouts, Rice has 243 yards, Worthy has 230, Tyquan Thornton has 219 but he's on injured reserve and nobody else has more than 65. It's a team that is a perfect candidate to try to turn around Brian Thomas Jr.'s career.

But the Chiefs also can't ignore the offensive line. Guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched for the second time this season on Sunday. Offensive tackle Josh Simmons has been a problem and was put on IR. Receiver would be the more splashy move, but adding to the offensive line might be even more prudent.

Biggest need: Interior offensive line, and maybe Jonathan Taylor too

Trading for Jonathan Taylor, which has been rumored, would be a big headline in Minnesota before the trade deadline. Taylor would obviously help, but it's not like there aren't other issues on the offense. Quarterback might be one of them but Minnesota isn't going to make a difference-making move there.

The Vikings could add Taylor and still have trouble blocking for him. They're thin at guard after Donovan Jackson suffered a torn meniscus in Week 4. Their starting guards on Sunday, Joe Huber and Will Fries, rank 33rd and 41st among guards in Pro Football Focus' grades. But, an upgrade like Taylor could make everyone look better. It would be a fun trade for everyone.

Biggest need: More defensive help, this time on the back end

The Bengals got the win in overtime Sunday and a bump up in the rankings, but there were some troubling signs. Tennessee's offense was one of the worst in the NFL and it gained 440 yards and scored 36 points on the Bengals. Given Cincinnati's defensive issues in recent seasons, it was worrisome even in the win.

"I know we have the guys in there that are happy we won, but they're not satisfied with our overall performance," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said, via the team's transcripts . "Each position group will go through that and find things we have to be better at."

The Bengals' line has been better with additions Dexter Lawrence II and Boye Mafe (Lawrence came up with huge plays in the win over the Titans), but the back seven could use some work. Help at cornerback or safety would be nice, and while the Bengals are trying to see it through with young linebackers Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr., they could use an upgrade there too. Cincinnati is a respectable 15th in defensive DVOA, but the difference between it making a deep playoff run or losing early on could be a defensive addition at the deadline.

Biggest need: Still defense, though the big move was made

The Bears' front office understood the assignment. Chicago traded two first-round draft picks to Tennessee for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. If there's a bigger move at the deadline from any team, it'll be a surprise. Simmons is exactly what the Bears' defense needed as a disruptor on the line, and he notched a sack in his Chicago debut on Monday night against Seattle . Chicago clearly feels like it's a contender now and was willing to sacrifice some high future draft picks for a shot at making a deep playoff run.

That doesn't mean the Bears should be done on defense, though any other move wouldn't be major. A mid-round draft pick for pass rushing help would continue to improve the defensive front. A reunion with Khalil Mack would make a ton of sense. But make no mistake: The Bears already made their all-in move.

"Super Bowl teams all have what we call a 'red-level' interior defensive lineman," Bears general manager Ryan Poles said of the Simmons trade, via the Chicago Sun-Times . "You need one.

"We've been searching, but sometimes the draft doesn't provide that to you. Free agency doesn't really [provide them]; it's very hard for guys to get out of the building when they have all of those things that we're talking about. [Simmons] was an opportunity that we had to jump on."

Biggest need: Offensive and defensive line help

The aggressive mindset that general manager James Gladstone wants to be known for will be put to the test. The Jaguars are one of the best teams in the NFL. Jacksonville has also dealt with two major injuries that need to be addressed.

Left tackle Anton Harrison tore his ACL in Week 5. Then defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton, who had been playing very well against the run this season, tore his quad Sunday and is done for the season. Walker Little has done a good job replacing Harrison, and perhaps that leads Jacksonville to look for offensive line depth rather than an impact starter. Replacing Hamilton with a high-end defensive tackle would be a strong move. Grover Stewart of Indianapolis might be a possibility, though the Colts might not want to trade within the division. If the Eagles trade defensive tackle Moro Ojomo, he could make a difference. It's time to see how aggressive Gladstone plans to be now that Jacksonville has one of the best teams in the NFL.

For once, finding weapons around Josh Allen isn't the top priority for the Bills. That has shifted to the defense. That group looked fine on Sunday, but that's because Lamar Jackson was knocked out after one play. Buffalo looked good against Baltimore's second and third quarterbacks, but the rest of the season has been rough. The Bills are 24th in yards and points allowed, and that's with an easy day against the Ravens included. Baltimore had 144 yards; Buffalo has given up at least 348 in every other game.

The Bills don't have the salary cap space to make a huge move on defense, but they should be looking into help at all three levels, with an emphasis on the back end. Only two teams are giving up more passing yards per game. Even if it's a mid-level move at cornerback or safety, the Bills know what they have to do. The Super Bowl window is wide open if the defense is good enough.

Biggest need: DeForest Buckner fills it, though maybe other moves are possible

The 49ers made a smart move to bring back DeForest Buckner in a trade with the Colts. Buckner might not be at his peak, like he was with his first go-around with the 49ers, but he's still a very good defensive lineman. The 49ers needed that. They also are hoping to get Nick Bosa back after the bye, which would be a big boost.

San Francisco has to weigh making improvements now for a team that has dealt with many injuries, particularly at receiver, vs. restocking with draft picks. The 49ers haven't drafted well in recent years and that has hurt their depth. That hasn't been a problem this season but it's looming. San Francisco also understands how a huge move can have a wide-ranging effect: A massive trade during the 2022 season for Christian McCaffrey boosted the team to a Super Bowl a season later and is still paying off. A trade for a receiver or defensive help would strengthen the 49ers' standing as the Super Bowl favorite, but they have to keep an eye on the future as well.

articles.title: Bears DT Jeffery Simmons gets huge sack in Chicago debut en route to win over Seahawks
articles.summary: It took very little time for Simmons to make an impact for Chicago.
articles.body:
SEATTLE — Just four days after heading to the Chicago Bears, Jeffery Simmons immediately made an impact.

Simmons, who was acquired by the Bears on Thursday in a big trade with the Tennessee Titans, made his debut in blue and orange in a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. And in the first quarter, the defensive tackle made a huge play, sacking the Seahawks' Sam Darnold for a 6-yard loss.

Unfortunately for Chicago, it didn't get to reap the rewards of the tackle due to a penalty. Grady Jarrett was flagged for a facemask that took place after the play, resulting in Seattle gaining 15 yards. But the sack counted in the books, giving Simmons his first big stat since changing teams.

Simmons finished with six total tackles, including three solo, in the massive win over Seattle . He also tipped a pass from Darnold that was collected by James Lynch for a game-sealing pick in the fourth quarter.

"It means a lot to me," Simmons said on the broadcast after the win, "to be able to play meaningful football."

The Bears paid up in order to get Simmons, sending Tennessee two first-round draft picks (a 2027 and a 2028) as part of the trade package. Chicago's defense has had its struggles, with the team allowing the most yards per attempt (8.7) in the league.

Despite the high cost, Bears general manager Ryan Poles said Friday that the team doesn't think of it as not caring about draft picks — or, as he calls it, the "F them picks" mentality. Instead, he touted Simmons' ability to make a difference both on the field and within the team's culture.

"I don't think it can be either or when you talk about a move this size," Poles said. "You need to have both. And that's what Jeffery does. We believe he's going to impact us at a high level on the grass but also in the locker room, too."
