articles.title: Eagles rumors: Landon Dickerson has drawn interest on trade market
articles.summary: As the 2026 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaches, fans of the Philadelphia Eagles have thoroughly discussed who should or shouldn’t be traded now that a pla...
articles.body:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaches, fans of the Philadelphia Eagles have thoroughly discussed who should or shouldn't be traded now that a playoff berth is all but out of reach.

With Cam Jurgens already gone , should the 2-6 Eagles approach the rare opportunity to load up on picks in an otherwise lost season with gusto, saying goodbye to more members of their Super Bowl core to try to build a new one? Or would it be better to hold onto Moro Ojomo and Riq Woolen now in the hopes of bringing them back in 2027, even if that would create more cap issues, instead of alleviating them?

While that opinion depends on the individual, on ESPN's The Aftermath, Adam Schefter revealed another Eagles stalwart on a long-term contract that other teams have inquired about: Landon Dickerson .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Then a couple of other teams that have really struggled, obviously, the Philadelphia Eagles are one," Schefter wrote. "I know they have some veterans on expiring contracts that teams would consider. Riq Wollin would be the kind of guy. Landon Dickerson, I know some teams have been interested in."

Ironically enough, Dickerson actually commented on the potential of being traded in an appearance on 94WIP, explaining that, at this point, trade conversations are part of the game, but he does love playing in Philadelphia and wouldn't mind being a one-team guy for his career .

"I mean, the thing is, the longer that you kind of stay in this professional athlete field, you do realize that there's really two sides to every organization. There's coaches and football players, and then there's front office stuff. I'm worried about playing football, and you just kind of have to come to accept that the trade stuff and everything, that's just part of the job," Dickerson said.

"When it comes to being in this career, in this profession is the trade stuff and all that stuff is, it's something you really, you can't focus on and worry about. And I feel the same way about it. I love this city. This right now is my home. I spend offseasons here. I love my teammates, coaches. I love everybody. And I really don't want to play for another team, but at the same time, again, that's not a decision that when it comes to trade stuff, you can make as a player, you don't just get to say, 'Well, I like being here, so don't trade me.'"

If a team came calling and would be willing to give up a solid pick for Dickerson, would Howie Roseman actually say no? Dickerson has spent much of the last two years dealing with injuries, and with his contract running through 2028 – with additional void years going through 2032 – if a team is willing to give up a pick for his services, it could make for a sound way to get better in the future before his play potentially falls off.

articles.title: Are Steelers a real-deal Super Bowl contender after dismantling Browns for first place?
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have moved to the top of the AFC North following their decisive 27-6 victory over the surprising Cleveland Browns in Week 8. Th...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have moved to the top of the AFC North following their decisive 27-6 victory over the surprising Cleveland Browns in Week 8. The Steelers appear to be responding well to first-year coach Mike McCarthy. They have won their last four games, and they are going to have a chance to get some rest and rehab during their bye week before they face their most critical game of the season when they go on the road to play the explosive Cincinnati Bengals.

If Aaron Rodgers can make the critical plays in that game and the Steelers can come away with the victory, they should have the inside track on winning the division. However, gaining the division title is not why Rodgers returned for his final season or the reason that McCarthy took the job that had belonged to Mike Tomlin for so many years. This team wants to have a deep run in the playoffs and add to the franchise's legacy as a Super Bowl participant.

A good season to this point does not mean that the Steelers will become a dominant team in the playoffs. The bigger question is how will the Steelers compare to AFC powers including the Buffalo Bills, New England Patriots, Jacksonville Jaguars, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The answer has not been determined yet, but the Steelers are on the right track, and if they are going to play with the best teams in the AFC and beat them, they are going to need Rodgers to finish the year in a powerful fashion, they are going to need Jaylen Warren to continue to provide a solid running game and an explosive finish from disappointing WR D.K. Metcalf.

This is a difficult season for Rodgers, even if he is leading a first-place team. He made up his mind that he is retiring at the age of 43 (as of Dec. 2) when this season concludes, and that means that he is thinking of his life past football. Perhaps his concentration remains at a high level on GameDay, but a part of Rodgers is thinking about how much more comfortable life will be when he is not taking painful hits on an every-game basis.

Rodgers' numbers are quite good this season as he has completed 175 of 288 passes for 1,871 yards with 13 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

Rodgers has been sacked 23 times, but the success of Warren in the running game can take quite a bit of pressure off of the quarterback. Warren has 704 yards on the ground, he is averaging 5.9 yards per carry and has scored 7 touchdowns. Warren is clearly having the best season of his 5-year career. He rushed for 958 yards last year, and he should blow by that mark well before December.

Metcalf is the Steelers' big-play receiver, and McCarthy will need more from him as the season progresses. He has caught 33 passes for 378 yards with just 1 touchdown. Those are ordinary numbers and if the Steelers are going to beat the best teams in the AFC, he is going to have to pick up his level of play.

The big advantage that the Steelers passing game has going forward is the play of their tight ends. Huge Darnell Washington has caught 19-254-3 and fellow TE Pat Freiermuth has caught 25-235-4. Freiermuth is an outstanding red zone and third-down weapon, and the closer the Steelers get to the most critical games of the year, the greater his focus is likely to be.

T.J. Watt and the defense is capable of dominating

The Steelers have been more than solid on defense this season. They are allowing 18.0 points per game and that ranks fourth in the NFL. They also rank sixth in yards allowed and third in rushing yards allowed.

While this is not the famed Steel Curtain defense, this unit can put its imprint on any game. The key is the relentless pass rush of outside linebacker T.J. Watt. He has 7.5 sacks, 9.5 tackles for loss, 3 passes batted down, 1 interception, 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery.

Every great defense usually has that one dominant player who can set the tone, and Watt is that player for the Steelers.

He also has key teammates that also contributing to the defensive effort. Two of those teammates are linebackers Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen. Wilson leads the Steelers with 69 tackles and he also had 7 tackles for loss and 3 passes batted down. Queen has 60 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 4 passes batted down and 1 forced fumble.

Cornerback Jamel Dean is something of a secret weapon for the Steelers defense. He has 30 tackles, 8 passes defensed, 1 interception and 3 forced fumbles.

While Rodgers and the offense are clearly going to have to step up if the Steelers are going to prove themselves as Super Bowl contenders, the defense is going to have to make multiple statements. Watt & Co. look like a unit that could get even stronger when the season reaches its most crucial moments.

The Steelers are not Super Bowl contenders yet, but they have the ability to climb the mountain and get there.

articles.title: Chicago Bears deliver statement win over Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks as Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons star
articles.summary: Jeffery Simmons stars on his debut for the Chicago Bears against the Seattle Seahawks in his first appearance since arriving in a blockbuster trade from the Tennessee Titans; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs
articles.body:
Williams was extremely efficient for the Bears (6-2) against one of the NFL's stingiest defenses, committing no turnovers, taking just one sack and throwing for 247 yards while completing 71 per cent of his passes.

Williams' play helped set up three short touchdown runs by D'Andre Swift and that proved to be more than enough against Sam Darnold and the Seahawks (4-4), thanks to the impact Simmons had on the defense.

Acquired last week from Tennessee for a package that included two first-round picks, Simmons took little time to make a big impact on a defense that had lacked difference-makers.

He had a sack on the opening drive, added another tackle for loss and finished with six tackles and a pass defended as Chicago held Seattle to 252 yards and one third-down conversion on 11 attempts.

The defending champion Seahawks lost for the third time in four games and are now looking up at the NFC playoff standings and can ill afford many more slip-ups. The loss ended a 30-game streak for Seattle in the regular season and playoffs - the fourth longest for any team in the Super Bowl era - of not losing by more than four points.

Sam Darnold went 17 of 34 for 188 yards and two touchdowns for Seattle, but his interception in the fourth quarter set up Swift's third TD that made it 34-17 with 4:41 to play.

The Seahawks struggled once again to run the ball despite their trade last week for three-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and the return of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price from injures. Seattle ran for only 81 yards.

The Bears started off well against Seattle's stout defense by putting together a 17-play drive on the opening possession to take the lead when Williams threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden.

The Bears added two more field goals in the first half and built the lead to 20-9 in the third quarter with another efficient touchdown drive that ended with a 1-yard run by Swift.

The Seahawks were bottled up by Simmons and the Bears for almost the entire first half before Darnold connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a 43-yard pass with 30 seconds left in the second quarter.

Things looked bleak for Seattle when Jason Myers had a 33-yard field goal blocked in the opening minute of the fourth quarter.

But DeMarcus Lawrence forced a fumble by Colston Loveland on the next possession that set up Darnold's 7-yard touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp, and Seattle converted the 2-point conversion to make it 20-17.

The Bears answered with another TD drive and put the game away after Darnold's interception.

SEATTLE — The Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football promised some prime-time drama. What followed was a surprisingly dominant 34-17 Bears win , a victory that exposed the cracks in the reigning Super Bowl champions and the normally impenetrable home environment at Lumen Field.

The Bears entered the game knowing that it would be a tough test. Chicago head coach Ben Johnson said he had "a tremendous amount of respect" for the Seahawks and quarterback Caleb Williams called Seattle a "worthy opponent."

Yet, it was one of the most dominant performances from the Bears all season, on par or a couple of strokes short of the jaw-dropping 59 points they scored in Week 1 at the Carolina Panthers.

Chicago scored 34 points against one of the best defenses in the league. The Bears' defense picked off the Seahawks' Sam Darnold and sacked him three times, and held Seattle to 1-for-11 on third downs. The Bears' special teams blocked a Jason Myers field-goal attempt in the fourth quarter and hit two key field goals of their own to stay ahead in the second quarter. Everything clicked, in all three phases of the field.

"How detailed we are, it's really cool to see those things come to life in big moments and just throughout the game," Williams said.

Part of that came as a result of the instant impact of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who was traded from the Tennessee Titans on Thursday. After a turnaround of three days, Simmons stepped into the Bears' defensive line like he'd always been there, getting a sack (on Seattle's fourth play from scrimmage), six tackles and a pass deflection.

Simmons said he was trying to stay in the moment, even as he went through the whirlwind of a near midseason trade. He traded his signature red sleeves — which he's said he wore so his 3-year-old daughter could recognize him on the field — for orange, and quickly tried to assimilate to a new life with Chicago.

"When I ran out of that tunnel, I just kept telling myself it's, it's just football. Go out there, be me, play by play, be in the moment," Simmons said. "It was a lot of emotion, and I'm grateful to be here and today was a great start."

That great start on defense included Cam Lewis' punishing — and legal — hit of Seahawks wideout Tory Horton on Seattle's first drive that ended in a three-and-out.

Williams and his offense followed by setting the tone of their own with a magnificent opening drive: 17 plays for 80 yards, shaving 8 1/2 minutes off the clock before finishing it off with a 1-yard Luther Burden III touchdown catch.

"That first drive, I thought our guys came out with their hair on fire and I think it carried over for 60 minutes," Johnson said in a postgame news conference. "There were some ebbs and some flows throughout that game, and yet it felt like we responded really well as a team and rallied together."

Simmons got to the Bears' facility late Thursday night, and immediately got to work, knowing he suddenly had to learn a whole new game plan.

"I was getting ready for the Cincinnati Bengals and I had to flip the chapter to get ready for the Seahawks. So it's all about being a pro," Simmons said. "I showed my coaches that this week that I'm prepared and ready to play, and they trusted me to go out there and make sure I was ready."

Williams was impressed by what he saw from Simmons while on the sideline.

"I'm happy he's on our side," Williams said. "He helps everybody on that field on the defense. He helps the D-line when he gets double team[ed]. He frees up other guys to be able to go be special, and then when he gets one-on-ones, [it] allows him to wreak havoc. And so, I'm excited he's on our team. He's a big key piece for us."

Simmons' readiness was clear to Johnson, who said Simmons "fit right in." That early dominance earned Simmons a game ball.

"His impact was profound," Johnson said.

'The reaction is the most important thing'

The Bears had plenty of things they prepared for against the Seahawks, including Lumen Field's famous crowd noise and the Seahawks' dominant defensive scheme. Johnson said the team had "one of the more elaborate game plans" for Williams to take on.

"It was a fun week," Williams said with a smirk.

Beyond juggling plays, Williams' confidence and composure held the Bears together on Monday night. After a lost fumble from tight end Colston Loveland — really the only significant mistake from Chicago's offense — led to a Seahawks touchdown, Williams spearheaded a response that led the Bears back into the end zone.

Williams went 24-for-34 passing for 247 yards and a touchdown, and took only one sack.

Williams said that he had told his teammates after the Bears' loss to the Green Bay Packers ( a humbling 31-7 defeat while Williams was out with a hamstring injury) that the way they responded was crucial to turning things around.

"When an event happens … the reaction is the most important thing, and that equals the outcome. And so, being able to react a certain way, being able to respond in a certain way, the way we did, is really important for us," Williams said. "We obviously don't want those things to happen, especially in those moments, but when [we] do, let's respond. Let's stay steady and be who we are."

Williams admitted that he didn't have a flawless game Monday. One mistake, a delay of game penalty on the way to the team's second-to-last touchdown, actually bailed him out after he'd misinterpreted a play-call.

"Luckily we got the delay of game, because I ended up messing up a little bit, and it allowed us a little bit more time to be able to fix it," Williams said. "The crowd was loud at that point and I missed a word, one word or so, and that's what happens."

Yet, the Bears kept going. Kalif Raymond rushed for a 39-yard gain as they repeated the third down, and D'Andre Swift finished things off with a touchdown that snuffed out the last of Seattle's comeback spark. It was Swift's second of three TDs.

"We didn't come here to make a statement," Johnson said of the Bears' victory. "We're still building, and this is part of that process right now and, and we've got a lot of really good pieces."

Though Johnson may not want to publicly admit it, this is a win the Bears can build on. Their 6-2 record is the team's best start since 2012; they've beaten tough and not-so-tough teams alike, without letting up on the gas.

And two of those "good pieces" — Williams and Simmons — shined.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford and wife Kelly's combined net worth: Inside their NFL earnings, podcasting success, luxury homes and the financial journey behind their family fortune
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford is worth about $180 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth, and the Los Angeles Rams quarterback has earned more than $400 million
articles.body: Matthew Stafford is worth about $180 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth, and the Los Angeles Rams quarterback has earned more than $400 million from the NFL alone. His wife Kelly has no verified figure of her own. A $55 million extension signed in May 2026 keeps him with the Rams through 2027. In June, the couple sold three Hidden Hills homes for $21.3 million. A California tax lien of $534,454 was reported in August.Matthew and Kelly Stafford’s combined net worth in 2026Start with the number that holds up. Celebrity Net Worth puts Matthew Stafford at $180 million and lists his 2026 salary at $40 million. Its tally of career earnings stands at $422.3 million.Kelly is harder to pin down. Estimates online run from $1 million to $12 million, and the sources behind them are thin. None cites tax records, contracts or business filings. Treat them as guesses.So a fair combined figure is “somewhere above $180 million,” with nearly all of it built on Matthew’s career. Kelly’s own income is real, but it has never been disclosed.The gap between $422 million earned and $180 million kept deserves a word. Career earnings are gross. Federal and state taxes, agent fees, and the cost of running a household of six take a large share. That is true of almost every NFL star, and Stafford is no exception.How Matthew Stafford turned NFL contracts into a fortuneStafford’s timing helped. Detroit made him the first pick in 2009, and he signed a six-year, $72 million deal with $41.7 million guaranteed. The league brought in its rookie wage scale two years later, which sharply limited what teams could guarantee to draft picks. He got in just before the door narrowed.After that, each deal reset his market. He signed a three-year, $53 million extension in 2013. A five-year, $135 million extension followed in 2017, and for a short time it made him the highest-paid player in the league.The trade to the Rams in 2021 changed both his career and his bank account. Super Bowl LVI came first, then a four-year, $160 million extension in March 2022 that included a $60 million signing bonus.His 2022 earnings listed at $61.5 million, his biggest single year.The last two negotiations are the most interesting. In 2025, the Rams allowed his representatives to look at options elsewhere, and the standoff ended with a reworked deal. Pay for 2025 and 2026 rose from $58 million to $84 million, an increase of $26 million. Then came his MVP season, in which he led the league with 4,707 passing yards and 46 touchdowns at age 37. The one-year, $55 million extension in May 2026 can reach $60 million with incentives.There is a pattern here. Stafford collected his biggest raises after proving he could still play, and he did it in his late thirties, when most quarterbacks are being managed toward the exit.Kelly Stafford’s podcast and the money behind the brandKelly started “The Morning After” in 2021. She talked about marriage, parenting and life around the NFL. Matthew appeared several times, including an episode recorded the morning after the Super Bowl win. Hank Winchester joined as co-host in 2023.Podcast income is rarely public, so any dollar figure for the show would be invented. What we can say is that it gave Kelly a platform and an audience, both of which tend to attract sponsors.That platform has gone quiet. Her last original episode came out on October 2, 2025. She said she needed a break for her mental health, and the pause stretched on. In a later Instagram Q&A she was unsure whether the show would return and blamed media attention for taking something away that she had built for herself.Her story stretches beyond the microphone. She was diagnosed with an acoustic neuroma in 2019 and had a 12-hour surgery that April. The couple have also pledged $1.5 million to the University of Georgia and $1 million toward an education center in Detroit.For net worth purposes, that history points to a simple conclusion. Kelly’s value to the family balance sheet is real but small next to Matthew’s contracts, and it is currently on pause.Hidden Hills homes, quiet sales and a tax lienReal estate is where the Staffords’ money is easiest to follow, and the record is more mixed than the headlines suggest.In Michigan, they sold their Bloomfield Hills mansion for $6 million in 2021 after listing it at $6.5 million. In California they bought a new Hidden Hills home for $19.6 million in May 2021 and sold it in June 2022 for $21 million. That was a gain of $1.4 million.Then came a buying spree. They paid $11 million in April 2022 for two homes that once belonged to Drake, which was $3.6 million over asking. They also paid $10.5 million that March for Wish Vineyards, an estate with a private vineyard. In December 2023, they spent $28.2 million on a newly built 15,000-square-foot mansion on land once owned by Jennifer Lopez.The June 2026 sales tell the real story. The Drake homes sold for a combined $11.6 million, a modest $600,000 above cost. Wish Vineyards went for $9.7 million, below the $10.5 million paid. Put together, the three sales brought in $21.3 million against $21.5 million spent. Before commissions and carrying costs, that is roughly break-even after four years.The family kept the $28.2 million home. In August, Page Six reported that California’s Franchise Tax Board had recorded a $534,454 lien tied to the 2024 tax year. It was unreleased at the time of the report. For a family with this income, that looks more like a paperwork issue than a crisis, though the reports did not explain it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Caleb Williams is MVP level and Chicago Bears are complete Super Bowl contenders after Jeffery Simmons trade, says Neil Reynolds
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears sent a statement to the NFL as they beat the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Monday night, underlining their own Championship credentials behind Caleb Williams; watch the Bears against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Sunday Night Football this Sunday, live on Sky
articles.body:
The Bears gave up first-round draft picks in 2027 and 2028 for a 29-year-old defender. They may believe that due to their successes on the field those will be late first-round picks, but it's still a big price for a player who is not exactly young in NFL terms.

That suggested the Bears believe they are all-in. They were 5-2 when they made that trade and they thought they could upgrade a defense that actually started this season pretty well but had room for improvement.

On Monday night the Bears backed up that big trade and maybe sent another message to the rest of the NFL and the viewing public as they went into Seattle and recorded an emphatic 34-17 win over the hometown Seahawks, and Simmons made an impact immediately. He led the team with six tackles, had a sack, two tackles were for a loss and he batted down a pass.

This Bears team more importantly looks complete now. They're led by a head coach who is imaginative, aggressive and has just enough crazy in him to keep this team on the edge in Ben Johnson.

Caleb Williams was excellent again in Seattle and he is elevating his game to an MVP level. It's never going to be easy going up against that Seahawks defense and not everything is going to be in structure.

If you move Caleb Williams off his spot he's going to be more than happy. So he had to work for his yardage on Monday night and it didn't look spectacular in terms of the box score - 247 yards, a touchdown, no interceptions - but it's what he did to keep this team energised, to keep them moving and his connection with his passing game targets continues to be at a high level and he has good weapons.

Rome Odunze, Colston Loveland and then Luther Burden has come on as a young wide receiver. Khalif Raymond always seems to come up with a big play when needed. The running game is there as well.

We're waiting for Kyle Monangai to come back from injury but D'Andre Swift had three touchdowns in Seattle, so this is a team that looks like they have all of the pieces in place now and they have belief.

If they didn't have belief they wouldn't be going out and making that trade for Simmons, and I think that's the other thing: this move sends a wave of confidence, excitement and energy through that Bears locker room.

They played that way on Monday in the toughest of environments and so now at 6-2 the Bears approach the midway point of this season in great shape, looking like they have every area of their team addressed and looking like they are very well led.

All of that is the tangible stuff but the intangibles are also important. These Bears feel really good about themselves, and feel good about where they are heading in the second half of the season.

They made progress last year in terms of making the playoffs and moving through the first round. This feels like a classic follow-up year where you can go deeper and put together a definite run and that's why those passionate fans in the Windy City are dreaming of a Super Bowl for the first time since and a Super Bowl win for the first time since the 1985 season.

articles.title: Week 9 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Lineup Advice, Stars to Exploit and Sleeper Options
articles.summary: Week 8 may have brought a little clarity to the NFL landscape, but it didn't do much to settle things in the fantasy football world. Unfortunately, it also brought more injury news, as Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson is set to miss an extended period with a thumb injury.
articles.body:
Week 8 may have brought a little clarity to the NFL landscape, but it didn't do much to settle things in the fantasy football world. Unfortunately, it also brought more injury news, as Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson is set to miss an extended period with a thumb injury.

Injuries will impact many lineup decisions in Week 9, though managers will only have to deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans being on bye. Still, playing the matchups will be important this week.

Here, you'll find some early start/sit advice for some Week 9 fringe stars, along with a few sleepers to consider targeting on the waiver wire. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver Broncos

Rostered in 57 percent of fantasy leagues, Denver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman may still qualify as a sleeper. However, that's likely to change after this week.

Coleman will continue to see a prominent offensive role after the Broncos placed fellow running back RJ Harvey on injured reserve . The rookie was Denver's top option on Sunday, and he rewarded managers with 20.4 fantasy points.

This week, Coleman could provide even more.

The Broncos are set to visit the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Carolina is coming off a long week and did a good job of containing the Green Bay Packers' ground game last Thursday. However, the Panthers have also surrendered more fantasy points to opposing RBs than any other team this season. The firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero probably won't change things that dramatically.

Sit: Derrick Henry, RB, Baltimore Ravens

The loss of Jackson will negatively impact Derrick Henry, who hasn't been the same weekly must-start he's been in years past. With backup QB Tyler Huntley also injured, Henry will be a very risky option on a short week against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The Jags will visit the Ravens on Thursday night.

Henry did find the end zone against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, which helped him to salvage an otherwise underwhelming (60 scrimmage yards) outing. However, he failed to reach double-digit fantasy points in the two games before that.

Given Baltimore's quarterback situation, Henry projects as a touchdown-dependent flex option in Week 9. That's both unusual for the future Hall of Famer and less than ideal against a defense that ranks first in yards per carry allowed and has surrendered just four rushing touchdowns all season.

Start: Caleb Douglas, WR, Miami Dolphins

The Miami Dolphins have relied heavily on rookie receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman Jr. this season. When healthy, Douglas has looked like the closest thing Miami has to a true No. 1 receiver.

The Texas Tech product has only been healthy for four games, but he has seen 19 targets over that span and has reached double-digit fantasy points twice. He delivered 8.3 fantasy points in Week 8, despite a matchup with star New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

Douglas delivered 21 fantasy points two weeks ago and could approach that threshold again in Week 9. Miami will host the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

Managers should view Douglas as a strong flex option this week, and he's a must-add where available. He's currently only rostered in 26 percent of leagues.

Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker was trending upward in a big way. He has solidified his status as Las Vegas' top perimeter threat this season, and he topped 20 fantasy points in both Week 6 and Week 7.

Tucker also had a fairly favorable matchup against a so-so New York Jets defense in Week 8. However, the Raiders largely ignored him despite engaging in an offensive track meet in New York.

Las Vegas relied instead on its ground game and a heavy dose of Brock Bowers to outpace the Jets 38-33. Tucker was only targeted once and was held without a catch.

Tucker will bounce back this season, but managers should try to avoid him in Week 9. The Raiders have a matchup with the San Francisco 49ers, who have been very unfriendly to opposing receivers this season. The 49ers are also coming off their bye and should have a great game plan in place to limit Las Vegas' passing attack.

Other Week 9 Sleepers and Waiver-Wire Targets

Gardner Minshew II, QB, Arizona Cardinals

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

Demario Douglas, WR, New England Patriots

Chigoziem Okonkwo, TE, Washington Commanders

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Hot Seat Check on Mike McDaniel and 4 Other Struggling NFL Coordinators
articles.summary: The midpoint of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, making for an ideal time to perform some temperature checks on coaching staffs around the league.
articles.body:
The midpoint of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, making for an ideal time to perform some temperature checks on coaching staffs around the league.

While most of the teams that have fallen well out of contention this early in the year will give serious consideration to a head coaching change in the coming months, there are a handful of organizations that stand to benefit more from a coordinator shakeup.

For clubs that still have a chance to make the playoffs or have entrenched head coaches with a proven track record of winning, it would be imprudent to go with the nuclear option of dismissing their leader.

The coordinators working under these head coaches aren't nearly as indispensable, however, and an in-season play-caller swap or even a dismissal could be in the works if they can't get things sorted on their side of the ball soon.

With that in mind, here's a hot seat check for five struggling NFL coordinators heading into Week 9.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may have secured a convincing win over the rival Atlanta Falcons and kept their playoff hopes alive and well in the unsightly NFC South race, but it's still fair to question offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's future with the franchise in the wake of the performance.

The most shocking aspect of Tampa's 16-0 victory was how it came without a single pass being completed by the winning team. Baker Mayfield started and played all 60 offensive snaps in the rain-soaked contest, but failed to connect on any of his three throws.

That's a stark regression from even Week 7, when Mayfield connected on just seven of his 11 passing attempts for a grand total of 64 yards. While Tampa won both games in blowout fashion, this sort of pre-merger style offense isn't sustainable and will be exploited by the far better defenses the team will face outside the NFC South.

While weather, Mayfield's thumb injury and some outstanding rushing work contributed to Robinson's decision to pound the rock relentlessly in recent weeks, the Bucs still need to prove they can pass the ball effectively at some point soon.

Mayfield has the talent to be an elite passer, demonstrating as much during an incredible 2024 campaign with current Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen running the offense. The veteran QB racked up an eye-popping 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns through the air that season.

The regression Mayfield has experienced under Robinson may be best visualized when extrapolating the passer's performances over his first five games of 2026 to a full 17-game season. Doing so results in just 2,308 yards and 10 touchdowns, a far cry from even the modest 3,693 yards and 26 touchdowns he recorded last year under former OC Josh Grizzard.

Robinson's seat may not be too hot quite yet, but the Bucs' schedule has some tough stretches in the back half of the campaign. If he can't find a way to jump-start the league's worst passing offense, it's hard to see him returning in 2027.

Al Golden's seat should be considered warm despite his team being right in the thick of the playoff hunt and pulling out a big victory over the weekend.

The Cincinnati Bengals' defense got off to a promising start to the 2026 season under Al Golden but has since regressed significantly, approaching last year's troubling levels of ineptitude.

Golden's tenure as Cincinnati's DC started off on a low note. After taking the reins ahead of the 2025 campaign, the former Temple and Miami head coach oversaw a unit that ultimately finished No. 30 in scoring and No. 31 in total defense.

The Bengals made some significant personnel changes in the wake of that disappointing 6-11 season, seemingly intent on avoiding squandering yet another season of star quarterback Joe Burrow's prime. Golden was retained in his same DC role, however, and that decision by head coach Zac Taylor could come back to haunt the franchise.

While the Bengals have flashed the ability to play better defense in 2026—most notably holding the Houston Texans to a meager six points in Week 2—they haven't done so with any consistency. With the team nearly losing to the lowly Tennessee Titans on Sunday, major adjustments are clearly needed to get this defense dialed in.

Golden's group allowed the Titans to score 36 points, far and away the most the hapless squad put up in 2026. Tennessee was averaging 15.4 points per game prior to Week 8 before ripping off three consecutive scoring drives to open the contest. If it weren't for the resolve of Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, it would have been an embarrassing loss to a foe that had already waved the white flag when it traded away top defender Jeffery Simmons earlier in the week.

Golden has failed to elevate this defense to even a league-average level by the season's midpoint. There's enough time to fix things—and a splashy trade deadline acquisition could greatly aid that endeavor—but Cincy's brass may have to consider a drastic maneuver if Golden can't find a way to orchestrate the turnaround himself.

The Dallas Cowboys suffered a disheartening defeat to the Arizona Cardinals this weekend. The loss not only dropped the club to 3-5 on the season and multiple games back in the NFC East race, but it could also prompt the dismissal of defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Prior to Sunday, the Cowboys boasted a 202-0-1 all-time record when leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter. That unbeaten run ended when their defense allowed the Cardinals to mount a furious comeback and prevail 33-30 in overtime.

The meltdown has every right to force owner Jerry Jones into a full-blown regime change, although it's far more likely that this Brian Schottenheimer-led coaching staff gets an opportunity to fix things by reallocating defensive play-calling duties or even replacing Parker with another defensive coordinator.

Parker has had a rough go of things since taking over the position earlier this year. The former Philadelphia Eagles' passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach is overseeing a unit that is giving up an NFL-worst 385.4 yards per game (including a league-high 152.8 rushing yards) and concedes a concerning average of 26.6 points per game—the sixth-worst mark in football.

Hopes that the defense may have turned a corner in recent weeks completely dissipated when Dallas was eviscerated by a pair of Arizona backups in QB Gardner Minshew II (who tossed three touchdown passes after taking over for an ineffective Jacoby Brissett) and RB Tyler Allgeier (who had 147 rushing yards on just 11 totes).

Despite a readily apparent need for sweeping changes in Dallas, Jones has long maintained his regrets about dismissing former coach Wade Phillips midway through the 2010 campaign. He echoed that sentiment on Sunday, expressing faith in Schottenheimer to turn the team around.

With Schottenheimer seemingly safe, Parker becomes the most obvious chopping block candidate and may be out before the month is over.

For the second consecutive season, the offensive coordinator role has become a serious problem for the Philadelphia Eagles.

While Philadelphia fans were largely relieved when head coach Nick Sirianni dismissed Kevin Patullo from his coaching staff after a rocky 2025 campaign, things haven't come anywhere close to improving under successor Sean Mannion.

Injuries have been the unfortunate story of Philadelphia's season, one that began with much promise but is almost certain to end with the franchise missing the playoffs for the first time since Sirianni took the reins in 2021.

Injuries aren't the sole reason for the squad's 2-6 record, however, as the NFC East-leading New York Giants have remained competent despite losing their star quarterback and several other key contributors early in the year.

Philadelphia was certain to regress with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the year, Saquon Barkley dealing with nagging hamstring and back issues and the offensive line getting gutted, but the offense now rates amongst the league's absolute worst following a six-game losing skid. Under Mannion, the Eagles head into Week 9 ranking No. 27 in passing, No. 27 in rushing, No. 30 in scoring and dead-last in total offense.

The Philadelphia Inquirer's Marcus Hayes cited Mannion as the Eagles' main problem over the past six weeks, highlighting the 34-year-old's lackluster credentials and inability to implement a cohesive scheme in his first ever stint as an OC.

With his unit scoring just 10 points against a sieve-like Washington Commanders defense that ranked No. 31 in scoring defense entering Week 8, it's become clear that Mannion isn't the right person to run this offense.

If Sirianni wants to save his job, he's going to have to cut ties and right the ship himself.

At this point in the Los Angeles Chargers' abysmal season, Mike McDaniel should feel fortunate to still have a job. Things have gone from bad (losing the opener against the Arizona Cardinals) to unfathomably awful (scoring just 15 points over the last two games) in the span of just two months.

While the Bolts entered the campaign as a dark-horse Super Bowl contender, they now must go undefeated the rest of the way to even finish slightly above .500.

A huge reason for this 0-7 start has been a complete offensive breakdown with McDaniel at the helm. L.A. ranks No. 28 in total offense and No. 32 in scoring offense under an offensive coordinator whose arrival was largely celebrated by Chargers fans.

The primary concern for L.A. during this collapse should be quarterback Justin Herbert's regression from fringe Pro Bowler to a borderline unstartable passer. If he continues to lose confidence, it's possible Herbert won't ever be able to regain the form he displayed earlier in his career.

Herbert has completed just 61.8 percent of his throws this year and is now averaging fewer than 200 yards per game while leading the league with 10 interceptions. Some of the signal-caller's decline can be attributed to an inconsistent, banged-up receiving corps that hasn't had Ladd McConkey at full strength for much of the year, but McDaniel's system doesn't appear to mesh whatsoever with the team's star QB.

Jim Harbaugh was asked by Fox's Eric Williams if he's considered making drastic changes such as benching Herbert or stripping McDaniel of play-calling duties, but the head coach declined to directly respond and said it will be a "team effort" to address the myriad of issues L.A.'s offense is contending with.

While that's not quite a vote of confidence, it appears the Bolts will be sticking with McDaniel for a little longer. Whether that will finally result in some victories or completely break Herbert remains to be seen, but the offensive coordinator's tenure looks unlikely to extend beyond the start of the 2027 offseason unless the offense improves dramatically.

articles.title: Mike Washington Jr. and the Best Week 9 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: With the 2026 fantasy football season now past its midpoint, it's become increasingly difficult to pluck worthwhile contributors off waivers. It's far from impossible, however, especially after an exciting NFL weekend featured a handful of unexpected breakout performances.
articles.body:
With the 2026 fantasy football season now past its midpoint, it's become increasingly difficult to pluck worthwhile contributors off waivers. It's far from impossible, however, especially after an exciting NFL weekend featured a handful of unexpected breakout performances.

While injuries are the main reason that backups tend to get elevated into a more prominent role at this point in the campaign, several coaching staffs opted to shake things up by giving a depth player more run than usual.

Mike Washington Jr. made the most of a surprise increase in playing time, helping guide the Las Vegas Raiders to a win with a steady rushing performance.

With Washington potentially supplanting Ashton Jeanty as Vegas' RB1, he becomes the most obvious player to make a run at this week. There are a handful of others—especially at the usually barren RB position—who also stand out, so with that in mind let's get into the top waiver-wire targets for Week 9.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros ' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (20 Percent Rostered)

The Dolphins may be a dumpster fire this season, but Willis has at least started flashing the talent that earned him a big contract in free agency with a bit more frequency.

Over the past three games, Willis hasn't finished below the QB14 mark. He posted his first two 20-plus point outings of the season on both sides of Miami's Week 6 bye, including a 26-point QB4 performance in Week 7.

While Willis unsurprisingly regressed with a 15.6-point outing against a stingy New England Patriots defense this past weekend, things look far more promising in the coming weeks.

The 'Phins have some premium matchups on tap that fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to capitalize on, starting in Week 9 when they face a dismal Detroit Lions secondary.

The Lions allow the most passing yards in football and subsequently rank dead-last in fantasy points conceded to QBs, giving up an average of nearly 25 PPG to the position.

With the Indianapolis Colts, Buffalo Bills and New York Jets (all ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in fantasy points allowed to QBs this year) representing Miami's following three opponents, Willis has the potential to be far more than a one-week rental.

If you are desperate for a QB, he's a serviceable choice to take your team into the fantasy playoffs.

Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (56 Percent Rostered)

The Raiders got back in the win column Sunday following a three-game skid thanks to a big outing from Cousins. The veteran's steady hand was instrumental in a 38-33 victory over the New York Jets, as he completed 19 of 26 passing attempts for a cool 247 yards and three touchdowns.

While Cousins' Week 8 passing volume was the lowest of his Vegas tenure, his efficiency resulted in a season-high 28.2 fantasy points and a QB2 finish—his best since Week 5 of the 2024 campaign.

While there was some speculation during the Raiders' recent losing streak that Cousins might cede his job to hyped rookie Fernando Mendoza, the outing should cement his status as Vegas' starter for a while longer.

With Cousins only posting two finishes outside the top 12 this season, managers shouldn't hesitate to put a claim in if he's available. You can deploy him with confidence in a Week 9 battle against the San Francisco 49ers.

It may not be an ideal matchup, but game scripting is likely to dictate a large volume of throws from the 38-year-old and keep him squarely on the QB1 fantasy radar.

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (9 Percent Rostered)

The G-Men turned their offense over to McCarthy in Week 7 and were rewarded with a shocking victory against a heavily favored Houston Texans opponent.

That win should strengthen his hold on the starting job for the remainder of the campaign, and the third-year QB could emerge as a sneaky-strong choice for fantasy teams needing to make a change of their own under center.

While McCarthy couldn't keep up the unsustainable rate of point production he displayed during a Week 6 relief appearance (he notched 17.3 points and a QB12 finish despite playing just 31 offensive snaps ), he still looked sharp against a tough Houston defense—completing 20 of 28 throws for 252 yards.

A lack of scoring plays and rushing contributions led to a pedestrian 10.2-point fantasy line, but better days are surely in store for McCarthy.

With Big Blue coming off a bye and set to face the collapsing Philadelphia Eagles, McCarthy has QB1 potential in Week 9. An extra week to glean more of New York's offensive system and build rapport with teammates he's only known for a month should pay dividends as the G-Men look to increase their lead in the NFC East.

Mike Washington Jr., Las Vegas Raiders (27 Percent Rostered)

Ashton Jeanty managers should be in panic mode right now, as Washington is on the cusp of usurping Vegas' feature back for more than just one game.

Washington shockingly earned the vast majority of carries during a 38-33 victory over the New York Jets and may have cemented himself as the Raiders' new starting running back. The sixth-round rookie finished the contest with 83 yards on 25 rushing attempts, while Jeanty only turned in nine meager yards on his two totes.

Jeanty should remain Vegas' main receiving back, putting a damper on Washington's PPR value. The rookie doesn't offer much in that area of the game and failed to record a single target against the Jets, but the drastic reduction Jeanty saw in both rushing volume and offensive snaps ( 25 compared to Washington's 38 ) has a real chance to become the new norm in Sin City.

It's too soon to tell if Washington will finish the season as Vegas' RB1 (or even come out of a Week 9 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers with that status), but the upside is far too alluring to pass up. Managers in all formats should make Washington a priority free-agent target this week, as there may not be another opportunity to scoop a true lead back off waivers this season.

Tyler Allgeier, Arizona Cardinals (52 Percent Rostered)

Arizona's backfield has been cursed for the past couple seasons and this hex continued in Week 8 when prized rookie Jeremiyah Love (who has already missed several contests in 2026) and veteran backup Bam Knight went down with respective ankle and concussion ailments.

Allgeier was the lone healthy back to finish the 33-30 overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys. He seized his expanded opportunity, racking up a whopping 36.1 fantasy points and finishing as the RB1 for Week 8.

The fifth-year veteran looked explosive on Sunday, gashing a weak Dallas defense for 147 rushing yards and a touchdown on just 11 totes. He also chipped in 44 receiving yards and another score on his five receptions. It marked a massive improvement for a player who was averaging fewer than three yards per carry coming into the contest.

With the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams and Kansas City Chiefs representing Arizona's next three opponents, managers shouldn't expect sustained RB1-level performances from Allgeier. He's still a fantastic waiver-wire add, however, as he'll command huge workloads while the rest of the Cardinals' platoon is banged up.

Kaelon Black, San Francisco 49ers (31 Percent Rostered)

Black entered San Francisco's Week 8 bye on the heels of a promising performance. He logged a career-high 31 offensive snaps in a 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons, taking over as the 49ers' top back while starter Christian McCaffrey was sidelined for a stretch with a hamstring issue. The rookie finished with 63 rushing yards and a score on 12 totes.

The last time Black saw more than 18 offensive snaps was in the opener, when he turned in 70 yards on 15 touches across his 28 offensive plays. It's clear he can produce when given the opportunity and would emerge as a solid RB2 if McCaffrey were to miss time.

While McCaffrey got some much-needed rest during the Niners' off week, hamstring issues are notoriously tricky and could continue to plague the superstar well into the back half of the season. Black was already a strong handcuff option in deeper leagues, but now needs to be rostered in most formats while McCaffrey's health looks murky.

Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (31 Percent Rostered)

Whispers continue to swirl around Jonathan Taylor's future with the Colts. The superstar could be the next domino to fall as the franchise—which already shipped off veterans DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson—continues its full-blown rebuilding efforts.

With the trade deadline just a week away, McGowan is the ideal speculative stash for managers seeking a lottery ticket at the RB position. There's a chance it doesn't pay off, but Taylor's potential departure would elevate McGowan to borderline RB2 status for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

McGowan has flashed a high ceiling during his limited usage, generating 163 rushing yards on 37 carries this year. Considering fellow depth option DJ Giddens didn't even see the field until Week 8, the seventh-round rookie figures to slot seamlessly into Taylor's vacated lead back role and would be in line for a huge amount of touches as Indy plays out the string.

Devin Singletary, New York Giants (4 Percent Rostered)

With Tyrone Tracy Jr. landing on injured reserve and Najee Harris released, Singletary should settle in behind Cam Skattebo as Big Blue's RB2 for the next several weeks.

Unlike the Seth McGowan suggestion above, managers will only want to claim Singletary if they believe a trade will not occur before the deadline. The G-Men have jumped out to a big lead in the NFC East race, however, and look like they could be buyers this week.

The backfield could clearly use an upgrade considering Singletary is set to play a large role, but there will be fantasy value here if New York stands pat and trusts the 29-year-old.

Singletary did have his best game of the 2026 campaign right before the Giants' Week 8 bye, recording 14.5 fantasy points with an efficient 5-41-1 rushing and 3-14-0 receiving line.

That RB22 finish is certainly closer to the veteran's ceiling than his floor, but it might inspire some front office confidence in Singletary. Deep-league managers seeking a flex-worthy player who should get approximately 10 touches per game could do far worse.

Jordyn Tyson, New Orleans Saints (51 Percent Rostered)

It's a tough week for teams in need of significant receiving help on waivers, but Tyson could be the savior managers are looking for.

The rookie has seemingly been on the cusp of making his much-anticipated debut for several weeks now, but the chances of him finally seeing the field look good for Week 9.

New Orleans is coming off a Week 8 bye that followed the team's trip to Paris to play the Pittsburgh Steelers. Although Tyson didn't play in that 16-10 loss, it was a promising sign that the No. 8 overall pick traveled across the Atlantic with the team.

On Sunday, ESPN's Adam Schefter provided another update regarding the wideout's Week 9 status:

Considering the Saints have been taking their time and not rushing Tyson back from a preseason hamstring injury, the wideout will be ready to hit the ground running when he does suit up.

Expect a fast start from a player projected to be a big part of the team's passing attack, with Tyson benefitting heavily from the defensive attention star teammate Chris Olave will command.

This is likely the last call on Tyson, who will get snapped up quickly as soon as his return is officially announced. Make a spot on your bench if you can, as his talent level and upside in Kellen Moore's offense create a situation where the wideout could emerge as a league-winner.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (26 Percent Rostered)

Williams is the next man up in a Washington offense that needs a playmaker to emerge in the wake of Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury. He got off to a decent start with a solid 5-54-0 showing on seven targets during a Week 8 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

While Williams' 10.4 fantasy points weren't a career-high, the rookie hasn't reached double-digits since his promising four-catch, 64-yard, one-touchdown debut in the opener.

With Washington's quarterback situation seemingly stabilized with a healthy Jayden Daniels again running the show, Williams has a chance to be one of the most improved players in the back half of the season.

Williams may not look like a strong waiver target at first glance, but his combination of upside and opportunity makes him one of the better wideouts you can stash right now.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (34 Percent Rostered)

The Cowboys may be collapsing with three losses in their last four games, but Flournoy has been surging up the team's pecking order and has clearly gained the trust of quarterback Dak Prescott.

Flournoy is well on his way to a career season, having tallied 30 catches for 342 yards and two touchdowns on the year. The third-year man out of Southeast Missouri State has been especially hot as of late, scoring nine or more fantasy points and finishing as the WR30 or better in four consecutive weeks.

Although a good chunk of Flournoy's production has been tied to scores—he's found pay dirt in two of the last three games—he's proving to be a reliable fantasy option. His ceiling may be limited if CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are both on the field, but he's generated four-plus targets in all eight games and has a stable floor. Consider Flournoy a perfectly viable WR3/flex option going into a plus-matchup against a weak Indianapolis Colts defense in Week 9.

Adonai Mitchell, New York Jets (11 Percent Rostered)

The trend of a different Jets receiver producing big fantasy numbers every week continued Sunday when Mitchell became the latest Gang Green pass-catcher to pop off.

The wideout racked up 142 receiving yards and a touchdown on seven receptions in a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, tallying a hefty 27.2 fantasy points and securing the first top-five finish of his career.

While Mitchell has dealt with injury (missing a month with a finger injury) and inconsistency (catching none of his three targets during his Week 7 return), he's an extremely talented receiver at his best.

Prior to landing on IR, the 24-year-old was Week 2's WR26, in addition to posting two top-15 finishes in a three-week span shortly after he landed with the Jets at last year's trade deadline.

Mitchell is a high-risk, high-reward waiver option heading into a Week 9 clash with the Kansas City Chiefs. He could put up week-winning numbers in the WR4/flex spot if he stays locked in, but he's also an obvious candidate to regress against one of the league's top pass defenses.

Mitchell could also take a backseat to teammates Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. again, so proceed with caution if you put a claim in.

Terrance Ferguson, Los Angeles Rams (16 Percent Rostered)

It's a pretty bleak week for tight end waiver targets when a player on the IR stands out as the best pickup. While managers can't feel too confident in any of the widely-available tight ends, Ferguson has far more rest-of-season upside than the rest.

Although Ferguson has been sidelined since Week 3 with a high-ankle sprain, he became eligible to return last week. As soon as he does get back on the field, Ferguson projects to assume a heavy workload in a Los Angeles offense that is hungry for playmakers.

With L.A.'s pass-catching corps dealing with several injuries, quarterback Matt Stafford was limited to a pedestrian 157 passing yards and one passing touchdown during the team's Week 8 win over the Chargers. Superstar wideout Puka Nacua (11-80-1 receiving) still managed to show out, but no other Rams wideout or tight end had more than two catches in the contest.

Prior to picking up his ankle injury, Ferguson flashed his immense upside during a nine-target, six-catch, 54-yard, one-touchdown outing in Week 2. Those types of performances could become standard when he's healthy again, making Ferguson a must-stash on any TE-needy roster.

Chig Okonkwo, Washington Commanders (30 Percent Rostered)

Okonkwo didn't have the best performance during Washington's big win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, but he'll have ample opportunity to get back to playing TE1-level football in the weeks ahead.

Despite the potential for an increase in usage with star wideout Terry McLaurin out for the season, Okonkwo only recorded two catches for 32 yards on four targets in Week 8. It was a disappointing showing from a player who went into the Commanders' Week 7 bye having tallied 13.9 fantasy points against a stingy San Francisco 49ers defense.

Don't give up on Okonkwo just yet, though, as Jayden Daniels only completed 16 throws in total on Sunday night. There should be plenty more targets heading the tight end's way as the team continues to sort out its post-McLaurin pass-catching hierarchy.

Mike Gesicki, Cincinnati Bengals (18 Percent Rostered)

The Bengals gritted out a thrilling overtime victory against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, a win that likely doesn't happen without a big game from Gesicki. The veteran finished with a modest four catches on six targets, but converted those grabs into 76 yards and a touchdown.

Gesicki's 17.6-point performance was a return to the quality form he displayed earlier this season. He notched three top-12 finishes over the first month of the 2026 campaign before sandwiching a pair of TE22 finishes around Cincinnati's Week 6 bye. The arrow is pointing upwards again for Gesicki, however, especially after Erick All Jr. was lost for the year with a torn ACL last week.

While seventh-round rookie Jack Endries saw some playing time and even vultured a one-yard touchdown on his lone reception of the year, Gesicki is firmly entrenched as the Bengals' top pass-catching TE. That role in Cincy's surging aerial attack makes him a good waiver choice for Week 9 and beyond.

articles.title: Former NFL star says he previously flew on private jet that crashed in Florida: 'Absolutely devastated'
articles.summary: Joe Mixon revealed he flew on the same Learjet 60 with the same two pilots just a month before the fatal Palm Beach County crash killed all nine aboard.
articles.body: Joe Mixon, a two-time NFL Pro Bowl running back, came to the harsh realization he had been aboard the private jet that plunged out of the sky and crashed onto a Florida highway. The former Cincinnati Bengals and Houston Texans star wrote on social media on Monday he was on the same plane about a month ago. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Absolutely devastated by yesterday’s tragic plane crash in Florida and the loss of all nine lives," he wrote on X. "I flew on that exact aircraft last month with those same two pilots. They were incredible professionals and genuinely wonderful people. Hearing the young woman’s story and learning about the bright future she had ahead of her makes it even more heartbreaking that her life was cut so short. "My heart, thoughts, and prayers go out to the grieving families and loved ones of everyone on board. A tragic reminder of how fragile life is. Love on your loved ones while you can, because you never know what tomorrow may bring." The Learjet 60 crashed in a Palm Beach County neighborhood on Sunday. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said Monday there were indications the jet was breaking apart before the fiery wreck and that investigators were zeroing in on weather conditions being a major factor in the incident. Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, 20, was the co-pilot, Jeff Gregory, 55, was the pilot in charge, Adam Robinson, 45, was a Texas tech entrepreneur and was traveling with his wife Helen Sharp and their two children and Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, who were traveling together and building their lives together. articles.title: Bears' Jahdae Walker Calls Out Seahawks With 1-Word Social Media Post After Statement Win
articles.summary: Chicago Bears wide receiver and special teamer Jahdae Walker summed up his team's decisive road victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears wide receiver and special teamer Jahdae Walker summed up his team's decisive road victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football .

Following the Bears' 34-17 win at Lumen Field on Seattle, Walker took to social media, making a one-word post on X:

"Belt" is undoubtedly in reference to the phrase "belt to ass," which has been popularized by Dallas Cowboys Hall of Fame wide receiver Michael Irvin and Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson when referencing a dominant win.

The numbers make it difficult to argue with Walker's assertion, as the Bears out-gained the Seahawks 363-252, won the time of possession battle 35:03-24:57, sacked Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold three times and held the Seattle offense to a third-down conversion rate of just 1-for-11.

It was a shockingly one-sided result given that the Seahawks were coming off their most impressive win of the season, holding the Kansas City Chiefs to three points in a 20-3 victory.

The Bears beat the Seahawks in all facets on Monday, though, and there is little doubt that new arrival Jeffery Simmons played a big role.

Acquired last week in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, Simmons had a sack in his Bears debut against Seattle, and seemed to open things up for the rest of Chicago's front four as well.

Simmons gives the Bears a menacing defense to go along with a dynamic offense led by quarterback Caleb Williams and head coach Ben Johnson, who calls the plays.

At 6-2, the Bears have one of the best records in the NFC, trailing only the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers.

Chicago is set to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next weekend, and a victory would send the Bears into their bye week with a ton of momentum and a four-game winning streak.

articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Rankings Guide for Top Players and Sleepers
articles.summary: It's hard to believe, but the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season is upon us. This means that fantasy football playoffs are right around the corner, and the final fantasy push has also arrived.
articles.body:
It's hard to believe, but the midpoint of the 2026 NFL season is upon us. This means that fantasy football playoffs are right around the corner, and the final fantasy push has also arrived.

Hopefully, you're still firmly in the mix for your fantasy postseason entering Week 9.

The good news this week is that we'll only have two teams on bye—the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans. The bad news is that injuries will still leave managers relying on sleepers at a few key positions.

Here, you'll find early point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for the top plays of Week 9, along with a few sleepers to target on the waiver wire.

After a rocky start to the season, Malik Willis has started to settle in as the Miami Dolphins' starting quarterback. He's appeared more poised in the passing game, and he remains a threat to chew up yards on the ground.

Willis recorded a solid 15.6 fantasy points against a good New England Patriots defense on Sunday. He also topped 20 fantasy points in each of his previous two games, and he could be back to that range against the Detroit Lions this week.

The Lions have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing QBs than any other team. Willis is only rostered in 22 percent of leagues.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Sleeper: Mike Washington Jr., Las Vegas Raiders

Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has dealt with ankle and foot issues for most of the season and has simply struggled to consistently find running room. He was far more productive as a receiver in Sunday's win, and the Raiders turned their ground game over to rookie Mike Washington Jr.

Washington logged 25 carries for 83 yards against the New York Jets. His PPR floor is somewhat limited because Jeanty is likely to remain the primary receiving back.

However, Washington logged 8.3 fantasy points against the Jets and could see a similar workload against the San Francisco 49ers this week. He's rostered in only 36 percent of leagues.

Sleeper: Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders

The Washington Commanders are coming off a decisive win over the rival Philadelphia Eagles, their first victory since losing No. 1 receiver Terry McLaurin for the season.

Rookie Antonio Williams played a big role in Washington's offensive game plan against Philly, leading the team with seven targets. He finished with five catches for 54 yards and 10.4 fantasy points. While the Los Angeles Rams will present a bigger challenge for Williams in Week 9, volume could push him to double-digit fantasy points again.

Williams is only rostered in 19 percent of fantasy leagues.

The Dolphins appear to be gaining some traction with Willis and their passing game, and it has benefited tight end Greg Dulcich. While rookie receivers Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman Jr. have become focal points of the offense, Dulcich has been a solid ancillary target.

Against the Patriots on Sunday, Dulcich caught four passes for 43 yards. He could be even more productive this week against the Lions.

No team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing tight ends than Detroit, and it isn't particularly close. Dulcich is rostered in only seven percent of fantasy leagues.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Cowboys cheerleaders crushed for dark & moody 'stripper' costumes, an odd free throw & Costco meal 'deals'

articles.body: Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. JERRY JONES SLAMS TABLE AFTER DAK PRESCOTT THROWS CRITICAL LATE INTERCEPTION IN BRUTAL COWBOYS LOSS These are very dark, very moody times for Jerry. This was supposed to be a huge month. The team has four home games at AT&T. The NFC East was his for the taking with the Eagles floundering and coming to town on Thanksgiving. "This is an indictment of the whole show," Jer told reporters Sunday night after a dark day in Cowboys history. "This is a criticism of everyone." DALLAS COWBOYS CHEERLEADER ALUM REACTS TO MY CHEMICAL ROMANCE GUN STUNT, RIC WILL BE OK & NBA FLOPPING "For our fans, we have to be better than that, where we got our hands on the win and then dropped the ball," Jerry added. While Jerry was dealing with disappointment, there was equal disappointment from fans of the Cowboys cheerleaders over the dark, moody costumes. "Costume malfunction they needed to have those pants elastic size underneath the boots . Also probably not a popular response, but they weren’t very becoming on some of the girls," one fan wrote on Instagram. "They’re beautiful that attractive ladies. My point was there could’ve been something else selected that would’ve made them look and feel a whole lot better." It was just a total disaster of a day for the organization. Fans really weren't into the "Stampede" look. "I’m shocked Kellie and Judy let them wear these," wrote another fan. Fans thought the outfits looked like something a stripper would wear. AMERICA'S BIGGEST BUFFET CHAIN CRACKED THE CODE TO ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT PROFITS "I really don't have a single issue with garters or strippers or the girls here, but the style of these outfits is just soooooo close to stripper outfits that it's simply a mindboggling match for good ol' Conservative DCC Land. As said: I don't care. It's just like cognitive dissonance by DCC, so my guess is that they want to sell more stuff to the 'male audience,'" wrote a concerned DCC fan. 📩 Email: joe.kinsey@outkick.comSend photos, stories, tips, rants—whatever you've got. 📰 Screencaps Page:👉 Read the latest Screencaps Congrats, we all made it to the finish line For those of us who live in battleground states, it's been miserable. Thank god it's over until the next cycle which will probably start in March. On Monday, I received EIGHT text messages from campaigns trying to get me to vote for them. I've also received two video messages from Archie Griffin telling me to vote. And, I'm not kidding, as I typed the last sentence, yet another text message came in telling me where to vote. Give me those Christmas commercials. The UK dummies celebrating this are some real morons The story of this guy who was walking around the world for 28 years is being hailed as some sort of accomplishment for humanity. Meanwhile, this loser left two kids in the UK so he could go for a walk. And I'm told he couldn't come back to see his kids because he would've broken his promise to walk around the world. Bulls–t. I'm also not convinced that this guy swam all the way across the English Channel. And what was stopping this guy from jumping on Zoom to talk to his mother? The BBC reported, "His mother, who had not seen him for a decade, told Bushby: 'Where have you been?'" I'm not buying any of this. The guy's a deadbeat. "Under the rules he set for his journey, he could not return to the UK to meet his family," the BBC added. "On rare occasions, he met his son and parents, who are divorced, in other countries." Costco 'deals' ranked in the modern economy for families that can't go to restaurants like the old days What other 'deal' am I missing in family ready-to-go meals these days? Ohio State coaching • Jack N. sent this to the Daily OutKick newsletter, but I would like to answer it: How can you explain Ohio State coaching, they were playing the 4th quarter like they were two touchdowns up. They continued to run the ball play after play and down 2 scores, well Day did it again, terrible play calling, he won the stats and lost by a lot, amazing. Kinsey: Two words - ARTHUR & SMITH. The guy thinks he's in the middle of an NFL season. There's zero sense of urgency. We've watched him not call a single play for Jeremiah Smith with the ball on the one-yard-line. We've watched him put the QB in the gun from the one-yard-line. I honestly have no idea how the guy keeps getting jobs. What was up with all the Michael Jackson Halloween costumes? • Gen X Warren has a theory: MJ Halloween costumes: one of my neighbor’s twin sons dressed as Thriller MJ and kids all around the neighborhood have been all about Michael Jackson playing the music. It’s because of the massive hit film earlier this year. It’s interesting to see Gen Alpha really embrace MJ. Kinsey: Kids were watching a Michael Jackson documentary? Warren, I want to believe you, but I'm not sure kids around here are sitting down to watch an MJ doc. This has to be something they're seeing on Fortnite, TikTok or some other game/app I don't know about. On modern grocery shopping and why college football is in trouble in certain towns • 'Sheriff' John in Houston adds his perspective: 1) On the groceries, we used to do the HEB curbside when the boys were younger, but that eventually just became its own PITA. When we did, I was always leery of letting them pick out my produce and fresh meat. Now we just make random grocery and costco runs when we need something or have decided to cook. Other than that, we eat out a lot and I see that getting even more frequent once the final child goes to college next year (I've noticed older couples eat out a lot). Personally, my preferred time for grocery shopping is 10:00 PM on a weeknight or 6:00 AM on a Saturday. Hate crowds. 2) On the college football question. First, OU is having a pretty bad season (except against my Longhorns) so you might expect attendance to be down. That photo might not be indicative of the whole sport. Second, big college stadiums are always slow to fill up pregame and that picture was obviously taken before kickoff. ALL THAT BEING SAID... I have noticed that my personal interest in CFB is waning. I still love gambling and staying up late drinking on the porch on saturdays, but the free agent / mercenary culture is really kind of off-putting. Those aren't "our guys" anymore, they are someone else's guys we are paying to come play for us. Texas is the worst. We can pay the most for players and we still have the same problems year to year. It does tend to strangle out the enthusiasm in the fans, at least for this fan, and I can really see how fans of the smaller poorer schools lose enthusiasm as well. As soon as you have some good players, they just leave. That would suck. So, to circle back on your question, I don't know if that particular OU photo means anything, but I do think the average fan is losing interest. Mac Tonight, Muppet Babies and the food Transformers were a big hit in my household #NotSponsored ################### SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER That's it this morning. articles.title: Caleb Williams Talks Jeffery Simmons Trade After Star's Bears Debut, 'Happy He's On Our Side'
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams loved his first glimpse of Jeffery Simmons along the defensive front.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams loved his first glimpse of Jeffery Simmons along the defensive front.

"I'm happy he's on our side," Williams told reporters after Monday's 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks.

Simmons finished with six tackles, including one sack and two tackles for loss. It was an impressive Bears debut for the four-time Pro Bowler.

Coach Ben Johnson singled him out for a game ball in the locker room during his postgame speech to the team:

Immediately after the Simmons trade, the general consensus was that Chicago made an obvious upgrade to the defensive line but paid a steep premium. It's a mixed bag in terms of NFL teams swapping two first-round picks for a proven star.

A blockbuster of this magnitude will ultimately be judged on what the Bears do in the playoffs. Even if Simmons performs at an All-Pro level, Chicago needs to make a deep postseason run to make the investment worth it.

On the basis of Monday night, that might happen.

articles.title: Russell Wilson private jet: Meet the $5 million Gulfstream IV aircraft reportedly linked to retired NFL quarterback

RW could be short for ‘Russell Wilson.’According to aircraft registration records, the private jet is registered to West2East 330 LLC, a Seattle-based limited liability company reportedly associated with Wilson.As per Seattle Times, Wilson purchased a 2000 Gulfstream G-IV, with FAA records listing the official owner as West2East 330 LLC, based in downtown Seattle. The aircraft was registered to the company in December 2020.According to AeroCorner, the Gulfstream IV was Gulfstream’s flagship in the late 1980s and 1990s. The SP version the 10-time Pro Bowler owns started at serial 1214 in 1993 and has a range of about 4,350 nautical miles.As per Celebplanes, the aircraft’s home base is King County International Airport in Seattle. The Federal Aviation Administration [FAA] issued the aircraft’s registration in December 2020. Its airworthiness date is April 2017, and it expires in December 2027.The 2000-built model is a fixed-wing, multi-engine aircraft with a capacity of over 22 seats. It weighs over 20,000 pounds and features a ROLLS-ROYCE TAY 611SER [Turbo-fan] engine, according to FlightAware.The aircraft’s thrust capacity is 12450 pounds. It can carry up to 14 passengers, cruise at around 500 knots, and fly roughly 4,200 nautical miles nonstop.The aircraft was originally priced at $26 million, but as of December 2025, the pre-owned Gulfstream IV jets trade between $3.5 million and $4.7 million.The aircraft is powered by Rolls-Royce engines and features a spacious, well-appointed cabin.
