articles.title: Jerry Jones Backs Cowboys' Defense, Unit is 'Getting Better' Despite Collapse vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner, president and general manager Jerry Jones offered a positive outlook Tuesday regarding his team's defense despite Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner, president and general manager Jerry Jones offered a positive outlook Tuesday regarding his team's defense despite Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

During an appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas (h/t Jon Machota of The Athletic), Jones said of the defense, "I like the way we're trending. ... I think it's better by what you saw Sunday in the first part of the game. It's looking that way with the future in mind that we can get better. And we are getting better."

Defense has been a consistent issue for the Cowboys in recent years, and that continues to be the case this season, as they rank last in the NFL in total defense and 27th in scoring defense.

Dallas' defense seemed to be heading in the right direction when it allowed just seven second-half points in a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7, followed by giving up only three first-half points against Arizona on Sunday.

Entering the fourth quarter of Sunday's game, the Cowboys had a 17-10 lead, and they went up 24-10 early in the fourth.

The Cardinals' offense exploded from there, though, thanks in large part to head coach Mike LaFleur making a quarterback change from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew.

Minshew threw touchdown passes to Tyler Allgeier, Trey McBride and Michael Wilson in the fourth quarter, and the only reason why Arizona didn't win the game in regulation was due to a missed extra point by Chad Ryland with six seconds left.

The Cardinals got the job done in overtime, though, as Minshew drove them into field goal range, and Ryland hit from 42 yards out for the win.

Dallas gave up 467 yards of total offense, including 202 on the ground, as Allgeier rushed for 147 yards and a touchdown on just 11 carries.

Since ranking fifth in both total defense and scoring defense under defensive coordinator Dan Quinn in 2023, the Cowboys have taken a nosedive on that side of the ball.

After Quinn became head coach of the Washington Commanders, the Cowboys were 28th in total defense and 31st in scoring defense under DC Mike Zimmer in 2024, and 30th in total defense and 32nd in scoring defense last season under Matt Eberflus.

Dallas pivoted to its fourth different DC in the past four years this season with Christian Parker, but things haven't gotten much better.

The Cowboys did bring in former NFL head coach and DC Mike Pettine a few weeks ago to serve as a senior defensive assistant alongside Parker, although it hasn't led to any significant improvements yet.

Three of Dallas' next four games are against the Indianapolis Colts, Tennessee Titans and Eagles, so while the matchups suggest that better times could be ahead for the defense, that unit has yet to prove it on the field.

articles.title: Predicting 2026 NFL Playoff Bracket After Week 8
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL playoff picture is far from crystallized, but the bracket is at least beginning to materialize after Week 8 wrapped up.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL playoff picture is far from crystallized, but the bracket is at least beginning to materialize after Week 8 wrapped up.

Legitimate contenders have started to separate from the pretenders after two months of play. A handful of teams have proven they have what it takes to navigate through the bracket and reach Super Bowl LXI, although things could change rapidly in the coming months.

Not every team that started hot will reach the playoffs. Teams that stumbled early can still recover. The journey ahead is filled with potential hazards that could cause even current one-loss programs to miss out on the postseason entirely. The road gets easier for several teams that would be on the outside looking in if the playoffs began today. It all sets the stage for a thrilling finish to the 2026 campaign.

With that in mind, let's break down the projected 2026 NFL playoff bracket, including seeding and record predictions for all 14 teams.

No. 2 Denver Broncos vs. No. 7 New England Patriots

No. 3 Jacksonville Jaguars vs. No. 6 Cincinnati Bengals

No. 4 Pittsburgh Steelers vs. No. 5 Kansas City Chiefs

The AFC side of the bracket is a bit more clear cut than its NFC counterpart. Only eight teams have five or more wins ahead of Week 9, while six have two or fewer.

The Bills may not be the most well-rounded squad in football, but they are still finding ways to win every week thanks to an MVP candidate quarterback and high-powered offense. If Josh Allen continues to put the team on his back and the passing defense can slightly improve after a rough start, Buffalo should cruise to the AFC's No. 1 seed.

Denver is surprisingly trending towards the No. 2 seed despite having the opposite problem of the Bills. The Broncos' No. 3-ranked defense is legitimate, but the Bo Nix-led offense is only averaging 273 yards per game—the third-worst mark in football. Head coach Sean Payton is still managing to get his squad up for quality competition, with Denver beating the likes of the Seahawks and Chiefs during its current four-game winning streak.

The Jaguars and Steelers round out the list of projected Wild Card hosts.

Jacksonville is far-and-away the class of the AFC South and is trending towards becoming the first team to lock up a divisional crown in 2026. Pittsburgh is hanging onto a slight lead in a much tougher AFC North race, although that competition has become a touch less fierce after star Ravens QB Lamar Jackson landed on the IR this week.

Despite a two-game losing skid, Kansas City is still well on track to make its 6-11 2025 season look like an outlier. Expect Patrick Mahomes and co. to figure things out and cruise to the team's 11th postseason appearance in 12 years.

Coming in just behind the Chiefs are the long-suffering Bengals, who picked up a big overtime win in Week 8 to remain on pace to return to the playoffs after a three-year hiatus. If Joe Burrow can stay healthy and the defense displays even moderate improvements, Cincinnati will have every reason to believe it can finally break through and win a Super Bowl.

The final AFC playoff spot winds up going to New England. The reigning AFC champions have regressed while playing a far tougher schedule this year, but there is still enough talent on both sides of the ball for this squad to reach the postseason. If Drake Maye can get back to playing anywhere near the MVP-worthy level he reached last year, the Pats will be dangerous come January.

Current records and playoff probability snapshotted after Week 8

No. 1 San Francisco 49ers (First-Round Bye)

No. 2 Detroit Lions vs. No. 7 Seattle Seahawks

No. 3 New York Giants vs. No. 6 Los Angeles Rams

No. 4 Carolina Panthers vs. No. 5 Chicago Bears

The NFC playoff race is shaping up to be an all-timer. With only five teams having secured five or more wins by the end of Week 8, all 16 franchises—including a trio of two-win clubs—still have at least a faint glimmer of hope to reach the postseason.

The 49ers took a commanding lead in the NFC West by jumping out to a perfect 6-0 record before finally suffering their first defeat in Week 7. Despite that small setback, San Francisco will have a playoff ticket punched and possibly even a first-round bye secured before the calendar flips to 2027.

The Seahawks don't seem nearly as inevitable this year. The reigning Super Bowl champions got off to a tepid start to their title defense and are in real danger of missing the playoffs entirely after tumbling back to .500 on Monday night. The club is far too experienced and talented to drop out of the running completely, but Seattle will probably begin its quest for back-to-back titles as a No. 7 seed.

The Rams are a slumbering giant that finally began to stir with back-to-back wins. After clawing back to .500, a second-half surge should result in L.A. clinching a respectable No. 6 seed. The door remains open for a potential home Super Bowl appearance at SoFi Stadium to end the season.

Detroit is on track to secure the NFC's No. 2 seed, remaining unbeaten in NFC North play. While the Lions started out with a modest 2-2 record, they are in the midst of a three-game winning streak that includes key victories over the Packers and Vikings. Don't be surprised if those wins end up settling some tiebreakers at the conclusion of the season.

The Bears struggled during Caleb Williams' brief absence, but the QB's return has sparked an offensive explosion. With Ben Johnson at the reins and key trade deadline pickup Jeffery Simmons bolstering the defense, the Windy City will inevitably celebrate a second consecutive playoff berth.

Rounding out the NFC side of the 2027 NFL playoff bracket are a pair of feel-good but ultimately toothless squads in the Giants and Panthers.

Despite losing Jaxson Dart for the year, Blue has still built a big lead in the flawed NFC East. While the G-Men have some sneaky upside if J.J. McCarthy can live up to his vast potential, it's hard to envision this squad being anything more than speed bump in the opening round.

Carolina is on pace to emerge from an atrocious NFC South race with both a losing record and a divisional title for the second straight year. While the team isn't a true contender, Bryce Young's ascendance at least gives this group a shred of hope in the Wild Card round.

articles.title: Jaguars are enjoying a home-field advantage missing for years, even decades
articles.summary: The Jaguars (5-2) are undefeated at EverBank Stadium this season and 10-1 there in two years under coach Liam Coen.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have a legitimate home-field advantage for the first time in years, even decades.

And there's only one explanation for it: These cats are clawless no more.

The Jaguars (5-2) are undefeated at EverBank Stadium this season and 10-1 there in two years under coach Liam Coen. The loss came against eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle in 2025.

The last time Jacksonville won more than 10 home games over a two-year span was during the 2006-07 seasons under then-coach Jack Del Rio. The Jags could end up topping that run with victories in their final three home games against Tennessee, Pittsburgh and Washington.

No one should be surprised to see it happen considering how the team has fared recently in its comfy confines.

Jacksonville has barely been challenged at home in 2026, beating Cleveland 34-10 in the season opener, routing New England 35-6 two weeks later and then dominating Indianapolis 42-7 on Sunday.

The Jags have won seven regular-season games in a row at "The Bank," outscoring opponents 271-75 in those outings.

"We want to keep doing what we do here at home and making it a hard place to play, as teams are seeing now," linebacker Foye Oluokun said.

Oluokun, fellow team captain Trevor Lawrence and teammates play their next three games on the road, beginning at Baltimore (4-4) on Thursday night. In fact, the Jags have seven of their final 10 on the road, which could make extending their streak at EverBank key to their playoff chances.

Playing well at home has created a rare and refreshing feeling for Jacksonville, which has finished below .500 at home in 11 of the previous 15 years. It's also a somewhat unexpected turnaround given the stadium is undergoing a $1.4 billion renovation that reduced capacity to 42,500 this season and a little more than 60,000 last year.

Nonetheless, it's not like the Jaguars are playing in front of roughly 80,000 like Dallas, Denver, Green Bay and Kansas City — or have the noise advantages of being inside a dome. This seems to be more of a supply-and-demand situation that caters to die-hard season-ticket holders.

The Jags also played two home games in London in 2026, which limited them to six regular-season games in Jacksonville.

"I think that's something these guys take a lot of pride in," Coen said. "They understand and feel the limited opps that we do have in this stadium, that we want to take advantage of those opportunities and jump out."

The Jaguars jumped on the Colts, scoring touchdowns on three of their first five possessions and opening up a 28-0 lead late in the second quarter thanks to backup safety Rayuan Lane's 92-yard interception return. It was the third-largest halftime lead in franchise history.

articles.title: Caleb Williams has arrived as a top-tier quarterback
articles.summary: Make room for the Bears QB in the Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow club.
articles.body:
In recent weeks, Simms and I have raised once or twice the question of whether Bears quarterback Caleb Williams belongs in the top tier of NFL franchise quarterbacks.

Based on Monday night's 34-point performance against a Seahawks defense that held the Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes to three points a week earlier, it's time to render a verdict.

The new top four, in our view, are (in no particular order), Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow, and Caleb Williams.

Lamar Jackson previously had been the fourth. A lost season due to multiple injuries puts him at No. 5, until he reestablishes himself in 2027. (And there's no reason to believe he won't, if he can get and stay healthy.)

In Week 7 at Seattle, Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. His passer rating for the game was 58.9. In Week 8 at Seattle, Williams went 24 for 34 for 247 yards, one touchdown, and no picks. Williams also sparked a 39-yard gain on a key third-down backward pass to receiver Khalif Raymond, which set up the score that turned a 20-17 margin into a 27-17 clincher.

And before anyone says Mahomes didn't have any support in the running game, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III and Bears running back D'Andre Swift averaged an identical 2.6 yards per carry against the Seahawks' defense.

So, yes, Caleb is a top-level NFL quarterback. Despite missing three games with a hamstring injury, his odds to win the NFL MVP award are down to 5-1, behind only Allen, Brock Purdy, and Burrow.

If the Bears keep doing what they did on Monday night — and if they finish the season with the No. 1 seed in the NFC — Williams will get plenty of votes. And he has a real chance to win it.

Even if he'd much rather win the MVP award not for the regular season, but for the Super Bowl.

articles.title: The NFL has a quarterback problem. The Ravens just became Exhibit A
articles.summary: Baltimore's nightmare QB situation exposes a much bigger NFL problem: In a league built around elite quarterbacks, there simply aren't enough capable replace...
articles.body:
The precise organizational term for the current state of the Baltimore Ravens is: screwed . It's a fate that likely awaits every other team that doesn't already have a quarterback succession plan in place, right this very moment. But Baltimore is uniquely beset by injury.

The Ravens lost all-everything quarterback Lamar Jackson on the very first play of Sunday's game against the Bills to a thumb injury that could cost him the remainder of the season . Making matters infinitely worse, Baltimore subsequently lost backup Tyler Huntley to a toe injury that could cost him time. And time is not a luxury Baltimore has right now; the Ravens are scheduled to play the Jaguars on Thursday night.

Oh, and just to add to the joy, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who leaped from emergency No. 3 quarterback into the lineup on Sunday, is himself dealing with an ankle injury. It rains, it pours, and sometimes, it Biblically floods.

As for Baltimore's quarterback options now, well … how's your arm feeling? Can you get to Charm City by Thursday?

The Ravens are in the teeth of the most vexing conundrum in the NFL right now: how to even survive, much less thrive, when your quarterback goes down. It's the most important position in team sports, by a wide margin, and consequently the most challenging one to fill. More complex offenses, more ferocious defenses, more pressure and more expectation all combine to forge a few elite quarterbacks, and shatter the rest.

You don't need any kind of advanced metrics to know what your eyes tell you: there are more teams in the NFL than there are good quarterbacks to lead them. The numbers back this up: ESPN's Total QBR stat , in this instance, is a useful benchmark. QBR doesn't simply total up yardage and touchdown passes; it incorporates a range of game situations and quarterback attributes, making it a solid starting point for discussions of elite, serviceable and unusable quarterbacks.

In the Total QBR system, a ranking of about 50 is average, and 25 is replacement-level. Players around the 50-point mark include Michael Penix Jr. (56.2), Sam Darnold (49.4) and Aaron Rodgers (49.2). So far, so good, right? At the low end of the 30 quarterbacks who have played enough to statistically qualify for the QBR leaderboard , you'll find Jameis Winston (41.4), Deshaun Watson (40.9), Daniel Jones (39.4) and Justin Herbert (32.6) — again, no real surprises there.

But when you look at the overall performance of all players who have taken snaps or thrown passes this season , that's when you really get a sense of how bad quarterback play can be. Fagnano posted a QBR of 7.4 in his emergency stint on Sunday. Tanner McKee is at 30.7 after starting, and losing, three games for Philadelphia. And Cooper Rush posted an almost incomprehensibly bad QBR of 4.7 — again, 25 is replacement-level — in his two losing starts for Atlanta earlier this season. The Falcons might have been better off just direct-snapping to Bijan Robinson every play, and the Ravens might need to consider the same route with Derrick Henry.

We can also determine the teams at most risk of a falloff due to quarterback injury by using a less scientific but more financially-motivated metric. Yahoo Sports' Ben Fawkes has created a list of NFL starting quarterbacks' value in terms of point spreads vs. their back-ups — in other words, the amount of value that a single starting quarterback brings to a team's odds — and, again, the results won't surprise you.

Per Fawkes' metric, the quarterback most important to his team's point spreads is — shocker — the Bills' Josh Allen, who's responsible alone for 7.23 points against the spread. Put another way, if Allen were injured and backup Kyle Allen needed to come in, any scenario where Buffalo was favored by fewer than +7.5 would immediately flip the Bills from huge favorite to pick-em status. That's pretty damn significant! Wrap Josh Allen in bubble wrap, Buffalo!

The next most important quarterbacks: Patrick Mahomes (backup: Justin Fields), Matthew Stafford (backup: Ty Simpson), and Drake Maye (backup: Tommy DeVito). Jackson comes in at fifth, responsible for 5.89 points against the spread, but that's with Huntley as his backup. Now? The gap might be double digits.

So you can see the problem here. There already aren't enough quality quarterbacks in the NFL, and the teams that have more than one in-house — looking at you, San Francisco — aren't parting with them for anything less than obscene ransoms.

Look upon the list of backups this year in the NFL , and despair. All due respect to Trey Lance, Quinn Ewers, Sam Howell, Davis Mills and the rest of the "hey, I remember that guy" guys holding tablets on sidelines across the league, but there's just not much there there.

The one hope that teams have is the Sam Darnold Scenario. Darnold, of course, sputtered from starter to backup, buried on San Francisco's depth chart until Minnesota resurrected his career and Seattle cemented his legacy with a Super Bowl title.

We have two extremely small sample size cases already this season: J.J. McCarthy, who seems rejuvenated with the Giants after flaming out in Minnesota, and Gardner Minshew, who checked in from 2019 to lead the Cardinals to a win over Dallas on Sunday. (McCarthy's QBR this year is 60.5 and Minshew's is 71.3, in case you were wondering.)

Beyond that, teams have to either mortgage their future with draft capital — say, overpaying for Kirk Cousins, if the Raiders were even interested in trading him — or grit their teeth and weather the storm until the offseason. When demand for quarterbacks far outstrips the supply, it's only a matter of time before someone — today, the Ravens; tomorrow, who knows? — ends up with nothing. That's the reality in a league now centered on, and entirely dependent on, elite quarterbacks.

articles.title: NFL Running Back Joe Mixon Flew on Same Doomed Plane a Month Before Fatal Crash
articles.summary: On social media, Mixon remembered the plane’s two crew members, who died alongside seven passengers in the Palm Beach, Fla., crash on Sunday, Nov. 1
articles.body:
NFL running back Joe Mixon says he flew on the same plane that crashed on Sunday, Nov. 1

Mixon shared a heartfelt post on X remembering the two crew members

Seven passengers also died in the accident, which happened on Sunday afternoon in Palm Beach County, Fla.

Running back Joe Mixon flew on the same plane that crashed on Sunday, Nov. 1, in Florida, according to a social media post he shared on Monday, Nov. 2.

"Absolutely devastated by yesterday's tragic plane crash in Florida and the loss of all nine lives," the NFL free agent, 30, said in a post on X . "I flew on that exact aircraft last month with those same two pilots. They were incredible professionals and genuinely wonderful people."

The Learjet 60 crashed on Sunday afternoon in Palm Beach County, killing all nine aboard. The crew included Captain Jeff Gregory and co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, 20, who was originally from Palm Beach and earned her pilot's license at age 17.

"Hearing the young woman's story and learning about the bright future she had ahead of her makes it even more heartbreaking that her life was cut so short. 💔" the former Cincinnati Bengals star wrote.

Filgueiras had logged more than 1,300 hours of flight time and was working for a charter firm based in Fort Lauderdale, her mother, Camila Corteleti, told The New York Times .

"She loved the freedom," Corteleti said. "It was completely different seeing the world from the top."

The jet took off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas on Sunday morning and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration confirmed to PEOPLE .

Seven passengers were killed in the crash. Adam Robinson, a tech entrepreneur, was identified as a victim in the crash, in addition to his wife, ceramicist and business owner Helen Sharp, and their children, daughter Emma and son Charlie.

Family members released a joint statement shared with PEOPLE and other outlets, which featured loving words to them and the other passengers, identified as family friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and the Robinsons' nanny, Anita Maria Cetina.

For Mixon, who missed the 2025 season with a foot injury and was released by the Houston Texans in March, the tragedy puts life in perspective.

"My heart, thoughts, and prayers go out to the grieving families and loved ones of everyone on board," he wrote. "A tragic reminder of how fragile life is. Love on your loved ones while you can, because you never know what tomorrow may bring.

articles.title: Five Eagles who could draw interest before the NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: Philadelphia’s 2-6 start could push Howie Roseman to consider offers for veterans and players approaching contract decisions
articles.body:
The Eagles' six-game losing streak has changed the conversation surrounding the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. Philadelphia must now decide whether short-term continuity is worth more than an additional 2027 draft pick.

Here are five players whose futures could be impacted over the next ten days.

Goedert remains a dependable target and one of the roster's most accomplished postseason performers. However, rookie Eli Stowers' emergence could make Philadelphia more willing to discuss the veteran tight end if a contender offers meaningful value.

Ojomo is playing on the final year of his rookie contract, and the Eagles have already made major financial commitments to Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. Ojomo has not recorded a sack this season, but he remains a useful interior defender who could strengthen a contender's rotation.

Smith is under team control through 2027 after Philadelphia exercised his fifth-year option. That control should increase his value. The Eagles should have little incentive to move him cheaply, but edge rushers routinely draw interest near the deadline.

Woolen's size, speed, and Super Bowl experience make him an appealing option for teams needing help at cornerback. Philadelphia must determine whether he fits its long-term secondary or offers a chance to recover draft capital.

Trading Baun would require a substantial return. He is a proven defensive leader and not an expiring-contract rental, but an aggressive contender could force Philadelphia to consider an offer that improves its long-term flexibility.

Howie Roseman should not conduct a clearance sale. The Eagles still need credible veterans around their younger core. However, standing still also costs Philadelphia if it loses players later without receiving comparable value.

articles.title: CJGJ Released by Bills After Serving 1-Game Suspension for Spitting at Raiders
articles.summary: C.J. Gardner-Johnson's time with the Buffalo Bills is over.
articles.body:
C.J. Gardner-Johnson's time with the Buffalo Bills is over.

Buffalo announced Tuesday it released the safety.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz initially reported the move followed his one-game suspension. Gardner-Johnson was given the penalty for a "spitting incident" during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders and missed Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens.

The suspension came after cameras captured him spitting toward star tight end Brock Bowers:

The veteran took to social media in the aftermath of the incident and apologized.

"My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," Gardner-Johnson wrote (h/t Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports). "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game. There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard."

Yet fines and punishments are nothing new for Gardner-Johnson, as Tim Graham of The Athletic noted he was fined 13 times for $194,924 coming into the season.

Gardner-Johnson, who led the NFL with six interceptions during the 2022 campaign on the Philadelphia Eagles, started six games for Buffalo this season and posted 26 tackles, two passes defended and one interception.

While there was a time in his career when he was a defensive game-changer, he largely struggled during his brief time in Buffalo. According to Pro Football Focus , his overall player grade of 55.2 ranks 71st of 98 eligible safeties for the 2026 season.

At 28 years old with plenty of experience under his belt following stops with the New Orleans Saints, Eagles, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans, Chicago Bears and Bills, Gardner-Johnson will surely draw interest from other teams looking for depth in the defensive backfield.

But he will no longer help the Bills chase a Super Bowl trophy this season.
